zh_title: “真实反映了他的罪行”：在国际社会的强烈抗议中，警方对活动人士黄之锋判处 10 年监禁表示欢迎
summary: 香港警务处国安处对黄之锋被判十年监禁表示欢迎，称这是反映所犯罪行的“适当刑罚”。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港警务处国家安全部总警司李锐周四在高等法院外对记者表示，希望这名活动人士刑满后能够正确了解中国，成为一个守法的人。黄伟
content:
香港警务处国安处对黄之锋被判十年监禁表示欢迎，称这是反映所犯罪行的“适当刑罚”。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港警务处国家安全部总警司李锐周四在高等法院外对记者表示，希望这名活动人士刑满后能够正确了解中国，成为一个守法的人。自 2020 年底以来一直入狱的黄在 9 月份承认与外国势力合谋罪名后，于周四被判处 10 年监禁。黄被指控在2020年与自我流亡的活动人士罗冠聪和其他未透露姓名的人士密谋，要求外国对香港和中国大陆政府实施制裁和封锁。活动家黄之锋于 2019 年 9 月 17 日在国会及行政部门中国委员会作证。照片：C-SPAN 屏幕截图。谭威廉法官周四表示，根据北京实施的国家安全法，此案性质“严重”，可判处至少 10 年监禁、最高无期徒刑。
当被《香港自由报》问及当局是否会上诉寻求更重的刑罚时，李说：“[判决]确实反映了他在这段时间内所犯的罪行，以及罪行的严重性。当然，我必须与司法部的同事讨论我们是否会[上诉]，但我个人认为这对他来说是一个适当的判决。”香港自由派获得了黄从监狱发出的一份声明，黄说，一名国安警察告诉他，他们是“敌人”。当被问及当局是否认为黄是敌人时，李说这不是他的观点。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋在高等法院宣判后，国家安全局总警司李志强向媒体发表讲话。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “我个人不会把他视为敌人。他是一个罪犯。作为警察，我们需要做一些事情来纠正这种情况并加强法律，”李说。行政长官李家超在周四的一份声明中将黄罗及其附属公司描述为“破坏香港繁荣稳定的罪魁祸首之一”。 “惩罚异见的工具”黄目前正在服刑四年零八个月，罪名是在具有里程碑意义的“香港47”案件中串谋颠覆国家政权，该案中45名著名的民主运动人士被定罪，并于2024年被判处最高10年监禁。
谭法官下令新的 10 年徒刑与他现有刑期的剩余两个月零两天同时执行。因此，这位 30 岁的活动人士将于 2036 年 11 月获释，届时他将年满 40 岁。2026 年 11 月 5 日黄之锋宣判后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。国际特赦组织在周四发布的一份声明中表示，香港当局将一名为权力说真话的年轻人定为罪犯。该人权组织区域副主任莎拉·布鲁克斯(Sarah Brooks)表示，这一判决“残酷地——也许是故意的——是在他根据之前的定罪获得释放的几个月前做出的。” “

【原文 English Original】
The National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force has welcomed the 10-year prison sentence handed to Joshua Wong , saying that it was a “proper sentence” to reflect the offence committed. Police officers outside the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Steve Li, chief superintendent of the National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force, told reporters on Thursday outside the High Court that he hoped the activist would gain a proper understanding of China and become a law-abiding person after serving his sentence. Wong, who has been behind bars since late 2020, was sentenced to another 10 years in jail on Thursday after he pleaded guilty in September to conspiring to collude with foreign forces. Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and other unnamed individuals in 2020 to request that foreign countries impose sanctions and blockades against the governments of Hong Kong and mainland China. Acitivist Joshua Wong testified before Congressional-Executive Commission on China on September 17, 2019. Photo: C-SPAN screenshot. Judge William Tam said on Thursday that the case was of a “grave nature” under the Beijing-imposed national security law, which warrants at least 10 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. When asked by HKFP whether authorities would appeal to seek a heavier sentence, Li said: “[The sentence] is truly reflective of his offence committed during the period, of the grave nature of the offence. Of course, I have to discuss with DOJ [Department of Justice] colleagues whether we will [appeal], but personally I think it is a proper sentence to him.” In a statement sent by Wong from prison and obtained by HKFP, Wong said a national security police officer told him that they were “enemies.” When asked whether authorities considered Wong an enemy, Li said that was not his perspective. Chief Superintendent Steve Li of the police’s National Security Department speaks to the press after Joshua Wong’s sentencing at the High Court on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I personally won’t regard him as an enemy. He is an offender. And as police officers, we need to do the things to rectify the situation and to reinforce the law,” Li said. In a statement on Thursday, Chief Executive John Lee described Wong, Law and their affiliates as “among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability.” ‘A tool to punish dissent’ Wong is currently serving a four-year, eight-month jail term for conspiracy to subvert state power imposed in the landmark “Hong Kong 47” case , in which 45 prominent pro-democracy campaigners were convicted and sentenced to up to 10 years in jail in 2024. Judge Tam ordered that the new 10-year prison term run concurrently with the remaining two months and two days of his existing sentence. The 30-year-old activist is thus due to be released in November 2036, when he will be 40. Police officers outside the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a statement released on Thursday, Amnesty International said that the Hong Kong authorities had made a young man who spoke truth to power a criminal. Sarah Brooks, deputy regional director of the human rights organisation, said that the sentence “cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction.” “Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security… Amnesty International reiterates its call on the Hong Kong authorities to overturn Joshua Wong’s national security convictions and to repeal all legislation that violates Hong Kong’s international human rights obligations,” the statement reads. ‘Properly understand’ China Having first emerged in the public eye as an opponent of a government-proposed national education scheme, Wong formed the student activist group Scholarism in 2011. He quickly rose to prominence as a youth activist, later becoming a key student leader during the 2014 Umbrella Movement. Nathan Law. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. In 2016, Wong co-founded the political party Demosisto with Nathan Law, who ran in the legislative election representing the party and was elected as the city’s youngest lawmaker. Li said on Thursday that Law, who now resides in the United Kingdom, should hand himself in to the Hong Kong police as soon as possible. The national security police chief also said that Wong had committed various offences since he began participating in social movements. Former Scholarism activists Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “He started taking part in the social movement whilst he was a youngster, and has committed various offences since his adulthood, including his offence under the national security laws, and the organising and inciting unlawful assembly, and also the contempt of law in various occasions.” “I sincerely hope that for the rest of his time in the prison, apart from reflecting on the wrongdoings he has done to the country and to the HKSAR, he must seize opportunities, to learn how to respect the law and to properly understand his own country.”

title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
zh_title: 美国中期选举对中美关系意味着什么
summary: 分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。投票结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，投票结果可能会对特朗普产生以下影响：
content:
分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。这次投票的结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，它可能会如何影响华盛顿和北京之间的棘手关系：关税会受到限制吗？分析人士表示，赢得美国国会参众两院的控制权使民主党能够限制特朗普在其任期结束后的两年内对中国产品随意征收关税。这可能对特朗普来说是一个潜在的打击，在双方达成休战协议（定于一月到期）之前，特朗普在激烈的美中贸易战中一直履行职责。上海复旦大学国际问题研究院院长吴心伯表示，如果民主党限制特朗普，这意味着他“在与中国的谈判中使用关税卡的能力将减弱”。 2026 年 5 月 14 日，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在北京人民大会堂会面。照片：中国外交部发言人毛宁，来自 Facebook。
然而，民主党人还必须权衡他们的行动与特朗普关税在美国企业中的受欢迎程度。新加坡南洋理工大学拉惹勒南国际研究学院高级研究员德鲁·汤普森表示，国会将“在未来两年内利用一切机会阻挠（特朗普的政策）”。但汤普森表示，民主党仍需谨慎对待进一步限制关税，这些关税“受到工会、蓝领工人和小企业的欢迎……他们历来是民主党的基础选民”。华盛顿布鲁金斯学会外交政策研究员帕特里夏·金(Patricia Kim)表示，国会将“不太愿意支持那些会急剧升级对华压力的措施，如果这样做可能会增加美国消费者和企业的成本或增加冲突的可能性”。台湾是“游戏规则改变者”？凯投宏观(Capital Economics)首席经济学家尼尔·希林(Neil Shearing)表示，台湾问题可能会“改变游戏规则”。台湾是美国支持的民主岛屿，北京声称拥有主权。华盛顿是台北最重要的安全支持者，已向台湾出售了价值数十亿美元的武器，台湾将用这些武器抵御中国潜在的攻击。但特朗普今年五月宣称美国对台军售可能成为与中国谈判的筹码，这让美国的立场受到质疑。此后，他的政府将一批价值 140 亿美元的武器推迟了数月。
台湾总统赖清德于 2026 年 2 月 11 日在台北举行的国防预算新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：台湾总统府。希林在一份报告中写道，中国可以利用特朗普总统任期的剩余两年加大对台湾的压力，特别是如果北京“判断华盛顿心烦意乱，或者特朗普愿意同意不干预的条款”。特朗普最近赞扬了他与中国国家主席习近平的“伟大友谊”，迄今为止，他顶住了民主党人和一些共和党议员的政治压力，

【原文 English Original】
A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say. Supporters cheer after the announcement that Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, former mayor of Atlanta, is projected to win the Georgia gubernatorial race during a US midterm election night party in Atlanta, Georgia, on November 3, 2026. Photo: Erik S. Lesser/AFP. Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing: Will tariffs be limited? Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say. That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January. If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. China’s President Xi Jinping (right) and US President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Photo: Mao Ning Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson, via Facebook. However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses. Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said. Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington. Taiwan a ‘game changer’? The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics. Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack. But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons . Taiwan President Lai Ching-te speaks during a press conference on the defence budget in Taipei on February 11, 2026. Photo: Taiwan’s Office of the President. China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package. But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said. “If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.” Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute. Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”. Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say. “Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim. “Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added. Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”. But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

title: Hong Kong lawmaker proposes digital ID checks for housing estate votes to combat bid-rigging
zh_title: 香港立法会议员提议对住宅区投票进行数字身份检查以打击串通投标
summary: 一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议采取了这样的形式
content:
一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议以议员议案的形式提出，该议案由议员提出，无意产生立法效力，但可能敦促政府采取具体措施。根据立法会文件，方建议研究利用政府的“iAM Smart”数字平台建立电子机制来核实和确认业主身份，“从而防止伪造、未经授权签署授权书以及滥用代理投票等问题。”未经授权的投票 2021 年 12 月的一次会议上进行的未经授权的代理投票帮助任命了宏福苑翻修工程的项目顾问，去年 11 月发生导致 168 人死亡、数千人流离失所的火灾时，该工程正在进行中。
项目顾问 Will Power Architects 此后被当局起诉，并与工程承包商 Prestige Construction & Engineering 一起被列为火灾背后的“罪魁祸首”之一。Christine Fong 于 2026 年 1 月 1 日宣誓就任香港立法会第八届任期。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大约四分之一的代理选票是由时任区议员黄佩琪 (Peggy Wong) 收集的，她因在庄园中的角色受到指控以及缺席议会会议数月后于 9 月辞职。然而，根据调查的最终报告，向独立调查委员会提交的证据不足以证明她参与了大埔住宅区的串通投标。周三，曾任区议员的方议员在立法机关发表讲话时表示，她知道有人以当时身在海外的房主的名义在她所在地区的庄园进行投票，而他们并不知情。她在意见书中还敦促政府建立黑名单制度，禁止被判串标罪的当事人提交涉及公共资金和补贴的标书，以及须接受强制检查的建筑物项目。她还建议研究建立匿名电子招标系统，并利用人工智能和大数据建立招标“异常警报”系统。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong lawmaker has suggested using a government-managed digital platform to verify property owners’ identities when casting their ballots in estate meetings, a measure meant to help prevent unauthorised proxy voting. Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lawmaker Christine Fong made the proposal at a Legislative Council (LegCo) meeting on Wednesday on combatting bid-rigging, an anti-competitive practice in the building maintenance industry that the city’s leader John Lee has moved to criminalise, almost a year after a deadly apartment complex fire in Tai Po. Her suggestion took the form of a member’s motion, a proposal introduced by a lawmaker that is not intended to have legislative effect but may urge the government to adopt specific measures. According to a LegCo document, Fong suggested looking into the use of the government’s “iAM Smart” digital platform to establish an electronic mechanism for verifying and confirming the identities of property owners, “thereby preventing issues such as forgery and unauthorized signing of powers of attorney and the abuse of proxy votes.” Unauthorised votes Unauthorised proxy votes cast at a December 2021 meeting helped appoint the project consultant for renovation works at Wang Fuk Court, which were ongoing at the time of the fire that killed 168 people and displaced thousands in November last year. Project consultant Will Power Architects has since been prosecuted by authorities and named as one of the “main culprits” behind the blaze, along with works contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering. Christine Fong is sworn in for the eighth term of Hong Kong’s Legislative Council on January 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. About a quarter of the proxy votes were collected by then-District Councillor Peggy Wong, who resigned from office in September amid allegations over her role at the estate and after months of absences from council meetings. However, evidence presented to an independent probe committee was insufficient to prove she was involved in bid-rigging at the Tai Po housing estate, according to the inquiry’s final report. Speaking at the legislature on Wednesday, lawmaker Fong, formerly a district councillor, said that she knew of votes being cast at estates in her district in the name of homeowners who were overseas at the time, without their knowledge. In her submission, she also urged the government to establish a blacklist system under which parties convicted of bid-rigging would be prohibited from submitting tenders involving public funds and subsidies, as well as projects for buildings subject to mandatory inspections. She also suggested looking into setting up an anonymised electronic tendering system and using artificial intelligence and big data to establish an “anomaly alert” system for tenders.

title: A Guide To China’s Expanding Fleet Of Military Helicopters
zh_title: 中国军用直升机机队扩张指南
summary: 中国人民解放军 (PLA) 拥有一支日益多样化的直升机机队，涵盖从基本飞行员训练和战场运输到空中预警、反潜战和专门攻击任务等各个领域。这支部队反映了数十年的发展，通常从从法国购买直升机开始，后来经许可生产，然后逐渐转向本土设计。结果是经过广泛现代化改造的旧飞机和围绕中国不断扩大的军事需求而设计的新平台的混合体，
content:
中国人民解放军 (PLA) 拥有一支日益多样化的直升机机队，涵盖从基本飞行员训练和战场运输到空中预警、反潜战和专门攻击任务等各个领域。这支部队反映了数十年的发展，通常从从法国购买直升机开始，后来经许可生产，然后逐渐转向本土设计。其结果是，经过大规模现代化改造的旧飞机和根据中国不断扩大的军事需求而设计的新平台，包括不断壮大的航母和两栖攻击舰队。 Z-10 攻击直升机。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images Z-8 系列最初源自冷战时期的法国 Super Frelon，是这种演变的一个特别好的例子。它催生了各种专门的变体，包括搜索和救援、运输、电子战和机载指挥所直升机。与此同时，Z-20（经常被称为西科斯基 S-70/H-60 克隆版）已成为具有陆基、海军和攻击型的现代中型运输平台，而 Z-10 和更新的 Z-21 则代表了中国对专用攻击直升机的日益重视。 2024 年，中国南方广东省珠海市的珠海航展上，一架 Z-8C 飞机进行空中攻击演示。
CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 本指南探讨了解放军运营的主要直升机类型、它们的发展以及它们预期发挥的作用。同时，应该指出的是，就目前情况而言，解放军在各种应用中仍然严重依赖外国采购的直升机。俄罗斯制造的直升机为解放军提供了运输和特种海军能力的结合。 Mi-17/171 Hip 系列支持部队和货物运输、搜索和救援、特种作战以及选择高空或特定任务角色。在海上，Ka-28 Helix 提供反潜战能力，而 Ka-31 的雷达则支持机载舰队监视。这些飞机仍在服役，其既定能力继续满足作战需求。然而，它们越来越多地得到中国设计的补充，包括某些专门为提供直接替代品而定制的设计。解放军运营的最先进的直升机是用于战斗搜索和救援的 Mi-171Sh。它具有广泛的自我保护设备和武器。摄影：Sun Lin/VCG via Getty Images 实用、训练和轻型直升机 HC-120 HC-120 是一款轻型通用直升机，源自 EC120，EC120 是中国、法国和新加坡在 20 世纪 90 年代共同开发的设计。
该型号于 2005 年进入解放军陆军航空兵服役，为初级直升机训练提供了现代化平台，并取代了老化的 SA316 Alouette III。HC-120 由一台透博梅卡 Arrius 2F 涡轮轴发动机提供动力。它的推出代表了陆军航空训练机队现代化的重要一步，为飞行员在过渡到更大的作战类型之前提供了使用更现代的直升机的经验。一架 HC-120，采用陆军航空训练学校的颜色。来自中国互联网 Z-11 Z-11 是由昌河飞机工业公司（CHAIC）和 602 研究所开发的轻型通用直升机。该设计基于法国 AS350BA Écureuil ，其示例来自于

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) operates an increasingly diverse fleet of helicopters spanning everything from basic pilot training and battlefield transport to airborne early warning, anti-submarine warfare, and dedicated attack missions. The force reflects decades of development, often beginning with helicopters acquired from France and later produced under license, before transitioning to increasingly indigenous designs. The result is a mix of older aircraft that have undergone extensive modernization and newer platforms designed around the requirements of China’s expanding military, including its growing carrier and amphibious assault fleets . A Z-10 attack helicopter. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images The Z-8 family, originally derived from the Cold War-era French Super Frelon , is a particularly good example of this evolution. It has spawned a wide range of specialized variants, including search and rescue, transport, electronic warfare, and airborne command post helicopters. Meanwhile, the Z-20 — frequently alluded to as a Sikorsky S-70/H-60 clone — has emerged as a modern medium-lift platform with land-based, naval, and assault variants, while the Z-10 and newer Z-21 represent China’s growing emphasis on dedicated attack helicopters. A PLAN Z-8C conducts an aerial assault demonstration at the Zhuhai Air Show in Zhuhai, south China’s Guangdong province, in 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This guide examines the principal helicopter types operated by the PLA, their development, and the roles they are expected to perform. At the same time, it should be noted that, as it now stands, the PLA remains heavily reliant on foreign-sourced helicopters for a wide variety of applications. Russian-built helicopters give the PLA a mix of transport and specialized naval capabilities. The Mi-17/171 Hip family supports troop and cargo movement, search and rescue, special operations, and select high-altitude or mission-specific roles. At sea, the Ka-28 Helix provides anti-submarine warfare, while the Ka-31’s radar supports airborne fleet surveillance. These aircraft remain in service where their established capabilities continue to meet operational needs. However, they are increasingly supplemented by Chinese designs, including certain designs that have been tailored to provide direct replacements. The most advanced Hip helicopter operated by the PLA is the Mi-171Sh used for combat search and rescue. It features extensive self-protection equipment and armament. Photo by Sun Lin/VCG via Getty Images Utility, Training, and Light Helicopters HC-120 The HC-120 is a light utility helicopter derived from the EC120, a design co-developed by China, France, and Singapore during the 1990s. The type entered service with PLA Army Aviation in 2005, providing a modern platform for primary helicopter training and replacing the aging SA316 Alouette III in that role. The HC-120 is powered by a single Turbomeca Arrius 2F turboshaft engine. Its introduction represented an important step in modernizing the Army Aviation training fleet, giving pilots experience with a more contemporary helicopter before transitioning to larger operational types. An HC-120 in the colors of the Army Aviation Training School. via Chinese internet Z-11 The Z-11 is a light utility helicopter developed by Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation (CHAIC) and the 602 Research Institute. The design is based on the French AS350BA Écureuil , examples of which were acquired for Army Aviation. Deliveries of the Z-11 to Army Aviation began in 1998. The helicopter is powered by a single WZ-8D turboshaft engine and is primarily used for training, liaison, and other light utility duties. A scout and armed reconnaissance derivative, designated as the Z-11WB, was developed with a nose-mounted electro-optical (EO) turret and external weapon pylons capable of carrying rockets, missiles, and gun pods. Its operational status remains unclear, although it provided the basis for the unarmed Z-11A training helicopter used by the Army Aviation Academy. A demonstrator for the Z-11WB scout and armed reconnaissance helicopter. via Chinese internet The Z-8 Family: From French Origins To A Modern Helicopter Lineage Z-8J The Z-8 was developed from the French SA321Ja Super Frelon, 13 examples of which China purchased during the late 1970s. Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation subsequently developed an indigenous version during the 1980s. Powered by three WZ-6 turboshaft engines, the original Z-8 became the foundation for a broad family of helicopters serving the PLA Navy (PLAN), Army Aviation, and People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF). The Z-8J is the naval transport variant, with a boat-like hull. For anti-submarine warfare (ASW) missions, the helicopter can be equipped with a surface-search radar, a French HS-12 dipping sonar, and Whitehead A244S or ET52 torpedoes. Several specialized derivatives were developed from the Z-8J: Z-8S: A naval search and rescue (SAR) version with upgraded avionics, a searchlight, a forward-looking infrared (FLIR) turret, and a rescue hoist. Most Z-8Js have reportedly been upgraded to this configuration. Z-8JH: A medical evacuation and SAR variant. The Z-8J and Z-8JH have both been used aboard Chinese aircraft carriers, providing transport and support capabilities for embarked naval forces. A Z-8JH on the PLAN replenishment ship Kekexilihu at Qingdao Port, Shandong Province of China, in 2023. Photo by Fu Tian/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images Z-8C The Z-8C represents a substantially improved successor to the original naval Z-8J series. The helicopter was first reported in 2016 and incorporates a number of changes intended to improve its performance and operational versatility. The most visible differences include a redesigned nose with a chin-mounted weather radar, a FLIR turret, and a pilot night-vision system (PNVS) mounted above the cockpit. A searchlight is also fitted, while the longer engine compartment accommodates the WZ-6C turboshaft engine. The Z-8C is operated by the PLA Marine Corps, while the Z-8CJ serves as a training variant with the Naval Aviation University. The helicopter has become a principal transport platform for the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, supporting the movement of troops and equipment between ships and shore. Z-8C helicopters conduct aerial display training for the upcoming Airshow China in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China, in 2024. Photo by Chen Xiao/VCG via Getty Images Z-8K/KA The PLAAF introduced the Z-8K in 2007 as a dedicated search-and-rescue helicopter. The related Z-8KA is configured for combat search and rescue (CSAR), including the recovery of personnel from hostile or contested environments. Both versions feature a FLIR turret, searchlight, radar-warning receiver (RWR), chaff and flare dispensers, and a rescue hoist. Some aircraft are also equipped with small terrain-following radars beneath the nose to support low-level operations. Selected helicopters have received satellite communications (SATCOM) antennas on top of the tail boom, improving their communications capabilities over longer distances. A further derivative, the Z-8KH, was developed for the PLAAF garrison stationed in Hong Kong. This version is distinguished by chaff and flare dispensers integrated into its flotation equipment. A Z-8KA helicopter during the 2022 Changchun Air Show at Changchun Dafangshen Airport, Jilin Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Z-8B The Z-8B entered service with PLA Army Aviation in 2011 as an improved transport helicopter. It shares several characteristics with the Z-8KH but lacks the latter’s flotation equipment. The Z-8B incorporates a glass cockpit and has become a major component of the Army Aviation transport fleet. Some aircraft have subsequently had flotation equipment reinstalled, reflecting the type’s continuing evolution. An optional auxiliary fuel tank can be installed inside the cabin to extend its range. Other upgrades have included SATCOM antennas on the tail boom and, on some aircraft, WZ-6C engines, an EO turret, and a terrain-following radar beneath the nose. A specialized operations variant has also been identified. These helicopters incorporate RWR, laser-warning receivers (LWR), and missile-approach warning system (MAWS) sensors, alongside flare dispensers and ceramic armor protection. A still from a CCTV video shows a Z-8B equipped with RWR, LWR, and MAWS sensors, as well as countermeasures dispensers. via Chinese internet Z-8G Lacking the boat-like hull of the Z-8B, the Z-8G is expected to replace that type in Army Aviation service. The helicopter was evaluated from 2014 and was specifically optimized for operations at high altitudes, including in Tibet. Unlike earlier Z-8 variants, the initial Z-8G configuration uses imported Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6B-67A turboshaft engines. Its redesigned nose is longer and more aerodynamically efficient, while the glass cockpit and terrain-following radar support operations in demanding environments. The helicopter also incorporates SATCOM and BeiDou/GPS antennas to improve communications and navigation during long-range missions. Some Z-8Gs have been equipped for special operations, with combinations of MAWS, RWR, and LWR sensors mounted on the rear fuselage and sponsons, together with chaff and flare dispensers. Armor plates beneath the cockpit windows provide additional protection, and some aircraft carry a 12.7mm machine gun inside a cabin doorway. Several specialized variants have also been identified: A battlefield electronic-warfare helicopter featuring large cylindrical antennas mounted on both sides of the mid-fuselage. Another electronic warfare configuration reportedly uses rectangular plate antenna arrays mounted on both sides of the rear fuselage. An airborne command-post variant featuring a retractable synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) surveillance system inside the rear fuselage, alongside additional electronic-support-measures (ESM) antennas. Some Z-8Gs may also have adopted the indigenous WZ-6C engine. A Z-8G at Airshow China at Zhuhai in 2024. Photo by Costfoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images Z-8L The Z-8L is a wide-body development of the Z-8G that first flew in 2017. Its most prominent feature is a pair of large sponsons mounted along the sides of the fuselage, providing additional space for fuel tanks and other equipment. The wider fuselage also increases internal volume, allowing the helicopter to carry more cargo and equipment. Relocating the internal fuel tanks beneath the cabin floor has further increased usable cabin space. Some aircraft have been observed with RWR and MAWS sensors on both sides of the forward fuselage, a roof-mounted FLIR turret, and a terrain-following radar beneath the nose. Additional defensive equipment, including LWR and RWR sensors and chaff/flare dispensers, can be installed on the sponsons. A SATCOM antenna is mounted on top of the tail boom. The original PT6B-67A engines are reportedly being replaced by the more powerful indigenous WZ-7 turboshaft. The Z-8L provides the Army with a larger and more capable transport helicopter suited to demanding operating environments and specialized missions. A Z-8L (nearest camera) alongside a Z-20 during the 2022 Airshow China in Zhuhai, Guangdong province of China. Photo by Stringer/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images Z-8D The Z-8D is a shipborne derivative of the Z-8L that first appeared in 2023. It combines the wide-body configuration with an extensive self-defense suite intended to improve survivability during operations over water. The helicopter features RWR, LWR, and MAWS sensors, along with chaff and flare dispensers. Four inflatable flotation units provide emergency protection in the event of a forced landing at sea. Power is supplied by either WZ-6C or the newer WZ-7 turboshaft engines. Engine air particle separators (EAPS) are installed ahead of the engine inlets to reduce the risk of damage from airborne debris. The Z-8D is expected to operate from China’s Type 075 amphibious assault ships and the larger Type 076 amphibious assault ship. One of the first clear images of a PLAN Naval Aviation Z-8D. via Chinese internet The Z-18 Series: Naval Utility, Early Warning, and ASW Helicopters Z-18Y Named White Heron, the Z-18Y was developed by the 602 Research Institute and Changhe as a new medium-lift shipborne transport helicopter. It is derived from the AC313 but incorporates a redesigned fuselage and a number of changes intended to improve its naval suitability. The helicopter uses imported PT6B-67A turboshaft engines and provides greater internal volume and payload capacity than the earlier Z-8. Improved performance in hot-and-high conditions is another important feature. The Z-18Y incorporates a nose-mounted weather radar and an FLIR/TV turret, along with additional communication and navigation antennas beneath the fuselage. A SATCOM antenna is installed on top of the tail boom. Folding main and tail rotor blades allow the helicopter to be stored more efficiently aboard ships. The Z-18Y is primarily used for carrier onboard delivery (COD) missions, transporting personnel and supplies between ships and shore. It has also provided the basis for several specialized naval derivatives. A Z-18Y operating from a Type 075 class assault ship. PLA Z-18J Named Bat, the Z-18J is an airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) helicopter developed from the Z-18Y. Its principal feature is a retractable radar antenna housed within a redesigned rear fuselage. The long-range, multimode AESA radar is lowered vertically during operation, providing 360-degree coverage around the helicopter. The Z-18J also incorporates a nose-mounted FLIR turret and additional MAWS and RWR antennas distributed around the nose and rear fuselage. Chaff and flare dispensers are installed in the flotation equipment. The helicopter has been used aboard Chinese aircraft carriers as an interim airborne early-warning platform and has also been observed operating from Type 075 amphibious assault ships. A rescue hoist is installed on the starboard side of the forward fuselage, allowing the aircraft to perform secondary SAR duties. An improved Z-18A features a redesigned engine and gearbox compartment and three indigenous WZ-6C engines. Some Z-18Js and Z-18As have also received SATCOM antennas to improve long-range communications. A Z-18J together with two J-15 fighters onboard the Liaoning . via Chinese internet Z-18F Named Sea Eagle, the Z-18F is an ASW and anti-ship warfare helicopter developed from the Z-18Y. It first appeared in 2014 and represents a substantial improvement over the earlier Z-8-based naval ASW helicopters. The helicopter incorporates a large surface-search radar beneath the nose, while its FLIR/TV turret has been relocated to the starboard side of the fuselage. A dipping sonar provides an additional means of detecting submarines, while MAWS and RWR antennas are installed on the forward and rear fuselage. Additional communications and navigation antennas are mounted beneath the fuselage. Four external pylons can carry torpedoes or anti-ship missiles (AShMs), including the YJ-9. A dispenser near the rear loading ramp allows the helicopter to deploy sonobuoys. The Z-18F operates aboard Chinese aircraft carriers and the Type 075 amphibious assault ship. Several improved derivatives have since appeared: Z-18FA: Incorporates a redesigned engine and gearbox compartment and three domestic WZ-6C turboshaft engines. Z-18FG: Features a new chin-mounted search radar and small side pylons for lightweight ASW torpedoes or AShMs. Z-18FB: A further improved version reportedly powered by three WZ-7 turboshaft engines, replacing the Canadian PT6B-67A. These developments point to a continuing effort to improve the Z-18’s performance and extend the operational life of the broader family. A Z-18F assigned to the aircraft carrier Liaoning . via Chinese internet The Z-9 Family Z-9A/B The Z-9 originated from the French AS365 Dauphin family, with China acquiring aircraft and subsequently producing them under license through Harbin Aircraft Industry Group (HAIG) during the 1990s. The Z-9A became a principal utility helicopter for Army Aviation and was also used for pilot training. The improved Z-9B incorporated a greater proportion of indigenous components, helping establish the foundation for China’s broader Z-9 development program, which also took it in a maritime direction. The helicopter has since become one of China’s most widely used light utility platforms and has also been widely exported in the Z-9E series. Cambodian soldiers stand in front of Z-9s during a handover ceremony at a Royal Cambodian Air Force base in Phnom Penh, in 2013. KHEM SOVANNARA/AFP via Getty Images KHEM SOVANNARA Z-9C The Z-9C is China’s indigenous naval derivative of the French AS565 Panther , examples of which were imported during the late 1980s. The helicopter incorporates a domestically developed surface-search radar and dipping sonar, allowing it to conduct ASW missions. It can carry up to two Yu-7K torpedoes and is equipped with inflatable flotation bags for emergency landings on water. Some Z-9Cs have been converted to SAR duties, receiving a searchlight, an EO turret, and a rescue hoist. The type has also been used for anti-piracy patrols off the Somali coast. In this role, some aircraft have carried a 12.7mm gun pod and a 57mm rocket launcher. A downgraded training version was developed for the Naval Aviation Academy. Z-9 sits aboard the Type 052D destroyer Zhanjiang at Ngong Shuen Chau Naval Base on Stonecutters Island in Hong Kong on July 6, 2025. Photo by AFP Z-9D The Z-9D is an improved derivative of the Z-9C, incorporating a greater emphasis on anti-surface warfare. The helicopter features stub wings capable of carrying up to four AShMs for use against smaller surface targets. A new fire-control radar is housed in a larger nose cone, while the weapon-control officer is positioned in the rear cabin. RWR antennas are installed on both sides of the nose and near the tail rotor. The Z-9D has been observed operating from Type 056 and Type 056A frigates. Some aircraft have also received an EO turret beneath the fuselage, expanding their surveillance and targeting capabilities. A Z-9D carrying a YJ-9 anti-ship missile. via Chinese internet Z-9F The Z-9F is an improved ASW helicopter based on the Z-9D. It was first observed in 2017 and is expected to replace the older Z-9C. The helicopter incorporates a new dipping sonar, a glass cockpit, and an improved surface-search radar. A BeiDou antenna is mounted on top of the cabin. The Z-9F retains the ability to carry up to two ASW torpedoes beneath its stub wings, providing a more modern platform for shipborne submarine-hunting missions. Z-9S The Z-9S is a naval search-and-rescue helicopter developed for operations aboard Chinese aircraft carriers. It features a nose-mounted EO turret, a searchlight, and a rescue hoist installed on the starboard side. The helicopter is also used for training by the Naval Aviation University. A small number of SAR-configured Z-9S helicopters are also operated by Army Aviation. A Z-9S conducts exercises onboard a Type 055 destroyer. via Chinese internet Z-9WA/WZ The Z-9WA is a night-attack development of the Z-9W, incorporating more powerful engines and improved avionics for operations in low-light conditions. The helicopter features stub wings capable of carrying up to eight KD-8 anti-tank guided missiles (ATGMs) or PL-90 air-to-air missiles (AAMs). A nose-mounted low-light TV/IR turret supports night operations, while RWR antennas are installed on both sides of the fuselage. Additional features include cockpit armor, flare dispensers, a datalink, and a redesigned cockpit compatible with night-vision goggles (NVGs). Z-9WZ. via Chinese internet The improved Z-9WZ incorporates a laser designator, allowing it to employ the newer KD-9 ATGM, as well as FN-6 AAMs. It is also powered by WZ-8H engines. Most Z-9WAs are believed to have been upgraded to the WZ standard. The PLAAF operates some Z-9WA/WZ helicopters in the SAR role. A similar derivative, the Z-9ZH, is used by the PLAAF garrison stationed in Hong Kong. Dedicated Attack and Scout Helicopters Z-10 The Z-10 represents China’s first dedicated modern attack helicopter. Developed by the 602 Research Institute, CHAIC, and HAIG, the program also received early input from Russia’s Kamov design bureau. The helicopter features a conventional tandem-seat gunship configuration, with the gunner seated in front and the pilot behind. A five-blade composite main rotor and distinctive scissor-type tail rotor distinguish the design. The Z-10 is powered by WZ-9 turboshaft engines and entered service in 2010, following its first flight in 2003. A Z-10K at the Shek Kong Barracks in Hong Kong, China. Photo by Zhang Xiangyi/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images Its primary armament consists of up to eight KD-9 or KD-10 laser-guided ATGMs, supplemented by a chin-mounted 23mm chain gun. The helicopter can also carry up to eight PL-90 AAMs. The nose-mounted PNVS and target acquisition and designation system (TADS)-equivalent housing incorporates FLIR, a TV camera, a laser rangefinder, and a laser designator. RWR antennas are installed on both sides of the forward and aft fuselage, while LWR sensors are mounted on the pylon tips. The initial prototypes were powered by the Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6C-76C engine. Series-production aircraft instead adopted the less powerful WZ-9, resulting in reductions to armor protection, sensor size, and weapon load compared with the original configuration. Several variants and upgrades have since emerged: Z-10H: Retains the original PNVS/TADS configuration while using WZ-9 engines. Z-10K: A dedicated version for PLAAF airborne units, featuring a new 23mm gun and 19-tube rocket launchers. Some aircraft have SATCOM antennas on top of the tail boom. Z-10A: The definitive production configuration, distinguished by upward-facing engine exhaust nozzles. Later upgrades: Some Z-10 and Z-10K aircraft have received additional ceramic armor, MAWS sensors on the nose, and SATCOM antennas for long-range communications. The helicopter has also gained newer long-range, IIR/CCD-guided ATGMs. These weapons require an additional datalink antenna mounted in front of the PNVS. Later developments include the introduction of millimeter-wave (MMW) radar-guided fire-and-forget missiles, potentially allowing the Z-10 to operate alongside the Z-19 in coordinated attack missions. The export-oriented Z-10ME incorporates further improvements, including a mast-mounted MMW radar. Z-19 The Z-19 is a scout and attack helicopter developed by HAIG using the H425 as its basis. It was intended to replace the Z-9WA while complementing the larger Z-10. The helicopter features a narrow fuselage and tandem cockpit, with the pilot seated in front and the gunner behind. A nose-mounted EO turret incorporates FLIR, a TV camera, and a laser rangefinder, while RWR antennas provide warning of hostile radar emissions. The Z-19 uses the same WZ-8C engines, transmission, and rotor systems as the H425, helping accelerate its development. A Z-19 without the mast-mounted MMW radar. via Chinese internet When fitted with a mast-mounted MMW radar, the Z-19 provides additional target-detection capabilities. The helicopter’s armament is broadly similar to that of the Z-9WA, including KD-9 and KD-10 ATGMs, PL-90 AAMs, rocket launchers, and gun pods. Later upgrades include MAWS sensors on the nose and tail, along with LWR sensors on the stub wings. The Z-19 has also been integrated with newer long-range IIR/CCD/laser-guided ATGMs, including the KF-9, KF-10, and KF-11. These weapons require an additional datalink antenna mounted on the nose. Z-21 The Z-21 is a new heavy attack helicopter first identified in 2024. Developed by the 602 Research Institute, Changhe, and Hafei, it appears to be a substantially larger and more heavily protected gunship than the Z-10. The helicopter is believed to use the WZ-10 turboshaft engines and rotor systems developed for the Z-20. It features a conventional tandem-seat configuration, with a gunner in the front and a pilot behind. One of the first photos of the Z-21. via Chinese internet Large cheek fairings on either side of the fuselage incorporate MAWS, LWR, ESM, and electronic countermeasures (ECM) equipment. The nose features a new PNVS above a TADS, while an MMW search radar is mounted above the main rotor mast. Laser-powered directional infrared countermeasures (DIRCM) are installed on the wingtips. Additional defensive equipment includes chaff and flare dispensers on the cheek fairings and tail boom. A BeiDou antenna is mounted on the tail boom, while at least one prototype has been observed with upward-facing engine exhausts. Z-21. via Chinese internet The Z-21 is expected to feature a 30mm chain gun beneath the forward fuselage. Each stub wing incorporates three weapon stations capable of carrying the newer KF-series long-range ATGMs, PL-90 AAMs, and other emerging weapons. Compared with the Z-20, the Z-21 is expected to offer improved high-altitude performance, greater armor protection, and a heavier payload, making it better suited to demanding attack missions. The Z-20 Family: China’s New Medium Helicopter Z-20 The Z-20 is China’s new medium-lift general-purpose helicopter, developed by the 602 Research Institute, Harbin, and Changhe since the late 1990s. The design is heavily influenced by the Sikorsky S-70 Black Hawk , examples of which China acquired for the PLA during the 1980s. However, the Z-20 incorporates a number of indigenous systems and is intended to replace the Mi-17 series in Army Aviation service. The helicopter features a five-blade main rotor, a glass cockpit, and armor protection around the cockpit. A PNVS is mounted beneath the chin, while RWR antennas are installed on both sides of the forward and rear fuselage. Additional equipment includes LWR sensors on both sides of the nose, SATCOM, ECM antennas on top of the fuselage, and a nose-mounted weather radar and terrain-following radar. A Z-20 during the 7th China Helicopter Exposition in Tianjin Municipality, China, in 2025. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images The Z-20 is powered by two WZ-10 turboshaft engines and can carry up to 13 fully equipped soldiers. An optional fuel tank can be installed in the cargo compartment to extend its range. Stub wings can be fitted to carry rocket launchers, gun pods, and external fuel tanks. The Z-20 first flew in 2013 and entered service with PLA Army Aviation by 2019. Several aircraft have been observed with upward-facing engine exhausts. A SAR variant incorporates an EO turret and searchlight beneath the forward fuselage, together with a rescue hoist above the cabin door. Z-20K/KS/KT The Z-20 has also spawned a number of specialized variants for the PLAAF. The Z-20K, identified in 2022, is a transport helicopter intended for airborne assault units. The PLAAF operates the Z-20KS subvariant in the SAR role. This model features an EO turret and searchlight beneath the forward fuselage, while optional stub wings allow it to carry rocket launchers and gun pods. An improved assault variant, the Z-20KT, incorporates a larger SATCOM antenna on top of the tail boom. Its folding tail section indicates that the helicopter is designed to facilitate aerial transport, allowing rapid deployment over long distances. A Z-20K at the Shek Kong Barracks in Hong Kong, China, in 2026. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Z-20T The Z-20T is a specialized assault helicopter broadly comparable in concept to the MH-60L Direct Action Penetrator used by the U.S. Army. The helicopter features large stub wings capable of carrying KD-9 and KD-10 ATGMs, KF-9A ATGMs, PL-90 AAMs, ECM pods, and external fuel tanks. LWR sensors have been relocated to the wingtips, while a TADS has replaced the weather radar in the nose. Additional armor plates provide increased protection for the crew and critical systems. Later examples have also been observed with upward-facing engine exhausts. Air Cavalry: Footage shows Z-20T assault helicopters effectively boosting the tactical flexibility of the Chinese PLA Army’s heliborne troops during an air assault training exercise. #Helicopter #AirAssault #Z20T #Z10 #PLA #Army #ChinaMilitary #ChinaMilBugle pic.twitter.com/NcoMbsz9gP — China Military Bugle (@ChinaMilBugle) May 1, 2026 Z-20F The Z-20F is a shipborne ASW helicopter developed to provide the PLAN with a modern equivalent to the MH-60R Seahawk . It first flew in 2018. The helicopter incorporates folding rotor blades and a folding tail boom to facilitate shipboard storage. An emergency flotation system is fitted, while the rear landing gear has been relocated forward to the rear end of the fuselage. The redesigned nose features an EO/laser-ranging turret, with a surface-search radar antenna mounted beneath the chin. A SATCOM antenna is installed on top of the tail boom. Additional ESM antennas are distributed around the nose and rear fuselage. A 25-round sonobuoy launcher is mounted on the port side, while a dipping sonar and rescue hoist provide additional ASW and SAR capabilities. The Z-20F can carry up to four YJ-9 AShMs beneath its stub wings, alongside lightweight ASW torpedoes on rear fuselage pylons. The helicopter is expected to replace the older Z-9C on Type 054 frigates and Type 052 and Type 055 destroyers. It has also been observed aboard the aircraft carrier Fujian and Type 075 amphibious assault ships. A Z-20F on the deck of the carrier Fujian carrying a pair of YJ-9 anti-ship missiles under one stub wing. via Chinese internet Z-20J The Z-20J is a shipborne transport and assault variant designed for the PLAN. Its stub wings can carry up to eight KD-9 ATGMs or four YJ-9 AShMs, as well as rocket launchers, external fuel tanks, and gun pods. MAWS sensors are installed on both sides of the chin and along the rear fuselage, providing additional protection during operations over water. The Z-20J expands the range of missions that can be performed from Chinese surface combatants and amphibious assault ships, complementing the ASW-focused Z-20F. Z-20J. via Chinese internet Conclusion Despite often being overshadowed by the PLA’s latest combat aircraft , missiles , and other high-profile weapons programs, helicopters remain an indispensable part of China’s military modernization. They provide critical capabilities, from moving troops and supplies across difficult terrain to supporting amphibious operations, special forces, search and rescue, and naval warfare. More importantly, the steady development of indigenous helicopter designs reflects China’s determination to reduce reliance on foreign suppliers and build a more capable, self-sufficient rotary-wing force. These aircraft may attract less attention than the PLA’s newest fighters, but their growing sophistication and expanding roles make them an essential part of the force’s ability to operate across a wide range of contingencies. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post A Guide To China’s Expanding Fleet Of Military Helicopters appeared first on TWZ .

content: 追光者報道 因民主派初選47人案服刑的前香港眾志秘書長黃之鋒，早前承認一項「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全」罪，案件今（5日）在高等法院判刑，黃之鋒被判入獄10年。黃自2020年11月起因其他案件一直還押，在獄中已接近6年。法官指在評估罪行的嚴重程度，須整體考慮案情，法庭認為本案屬「罪行重大」。 黃之鋒今日步入法庭時，戴着黑框眼鏡，手拿筆記和一本書，在犯人欄坐下後向旁聽的公眾人士點頭，並做出OK的手勢。法官強調，黃之鋒並非因《國安法》生效前的行為或政治理念而被判刑，在法例生效後黃之鋒及羅冠聰等人繼續共同履行協議，黃留港繼續支持「國際線」，包括在社交平台分享羅的帖文。而法例生效前的行為和活動，則構成罪行的背景。 法庭認為本案局「罪行重大」，案發時社會動盪、法治面臨重大風險，指黃之鋒和羅冠聰呼籲制裁，加劇港府及中國當時的處境。報道指黃之鋒聽到後表情平靜，繼續低頭抄寫筆記。 黃之鋒被控於2020年7月1日至11月23日間，在香港與羅冠聰及其他身分不詳的人串謀請求外國或者境外機構、組織、人員實施對香港特別行政區或者中華人民共和國制裁、封鎖或者採取其他敵對行動。並且在《國安法》實施前後，二人及香港眾志多次呼籲外國對香港特區及中國採取制裁或敵對措施，包括訪問外國、會見政界人士、參與聽證會、發起聯署，以及在社交媒體和外國媒體上倡議「國際線」。 案情又指多國針對中國及香港特區政府採取措施，包括美國通過《香港自治法案》、制裁政府官員及暫停部分協議，英國、德國、法國亦暫停與香港的引渡逃犯協議。 黃之鋒在2025年6月6日因本案被捕，當時他正在獄中就「47人案」而服刑。上月剛踏入30歲的黃之鋒自2020年11月起一直被囚。他於「47人案」被判入獄4年8個月，原預計明年1月出獄，而今次刑期為10年，其中2個月會與「47人案」同期執行，料最快2036年11月才能刑滿出獄。 國際人權組織持續關注案件 黃之鋒被控勾結境外勢力罪一直受到國際人權組織關注，有組織指出港府的指控在2020年取消他的參選資格時，同時指他勾結外國勢力，顯示其後針對他的《國安法》指控早在提出控罪前已決定。港府亦將對法治和人權狀況的監察，定性為對國家主權的攻擊。控方又將黃之鋒在國際的倡議活動，描述為促請外國實施制裁，卻刻意忽略他曾大力聲援2020年8月遭中國海警截獲及拘留的12名抗爭者，意圖抹去其人權背景。 而針對被捕和控罪時間點，案中所涉及的行為可追溯至2020年，但黃直至2025年6月才因相關案件被捕。當時他已就「初選47人案」服了大部分刑期。因此，人權組織認為當局在他預計於明年1月獲釋前夕，對他提出新的檢控。 香港眾志於2016年成立，而黃之鋒及羅冠聰分別曾任秘書長及創黨主席，至2020年6月30日該組織解散，羅冠聰其後離港。案情指黃之鋒在《國安法》生效前串謀勾結外國勢力的行為，黃之鋒、羅冠聰及香港眾志於2016年參與推動美國的《香港人權與民主法案》；2019年出席「美國國會及行政當局中國委員會」聽證會，提及該年社會運動狀況，要求重新審視美國給予香港的特殊待遇地位；同年與德國時任外交部長馬斯見面，促請德國延遲與中國和香港的貿易、停止向香港警察售武。 而在《國安法》生效後的行為包括黃在眾志解散後，在Facebook稱不會刪除舊文、不會放棄其政治立場和意見，亦不會放棄打「國際線」。而其身在海外的戰友，例如羅冠聰將繼續打「國際線」、代替因《國安法》而未能在港提出的主張，認為香港需要有人留守，在本地繼續抗爭、爭取國際社會和外媒關注。

title: 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別
summary: 追光者 2026-11-5 【 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別 】 席捲整個法國的示威浪潮持續，全國周四（6日）有多達200場示威。今波抗爭始於高中生不滿政府對教育撥款不足，不過到工會「接力」時卻加入調高最低工資等訴求，這是一場「騎劫」嗎？香港主流傳媒亦藉法國今場抗爭與7年前的「反送中運動」相提並論，兩者又有可比性嗎？ 法國高中學生面對教師不足、校舍老鼠為患，甚至連桌椅都欠缺的學習環境，於是近月憤而以堵塞校園、上街示威等手段表達不滿。
content: 追光者  2026-11-5 【 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別 】 席捲整個法國的示威浪潮持續，全國周四（6日）有多達200場示威。今波抗爭始於高中生不滿政府對教育撥款不足，不過到工會「接力」時卻加入調高最低工資等訴求，這是一場「騎劫」嗎？香港主流傳媒亦藉法國今場抗爭與7年前的「反送中運動」相提並論，兩者又有可比性嗎？ 法國高中學生面對教師不足、校舍老鼠為患，甚至連桌椅都欠缺的學習環境，於是近月憤而以堵塞校園、上街示威等手段表達不滿。不過工會周四發起的大罷工，雖然一方面聲稱是要聲援學生抗爭，但另一方面同時加入了爭取提高最低工資、要求政府修訂財政預算等訴求。 法國全國總工會（CGT）亞洲及大洋洲地區經濟政策顧問 Sylvain Goldstein 周四遊行前接受《追光者》訪問，被問到工會加入會否令學生訴求失焦時，強調兩個群體的訴求背後是源於同一個問題，「如果你（打工仔）有好的薪酬，他們就可以負擔社會保障費（social contribution），可以買椅子、書桌、為教師支薪；但如果人工低，就不能買不同的東西」。 那高中生會認為自己的貢獻被「騎劫」嗎？與朋友參與示威的 Rose 交代自己為何參與遊行時，卻表示自己是為展示與法國勞動階層的團結所以走上街頭：「因為我們其實正陷於經濟危機，即是政府不能滿足我們的期望，像我們1968年5月還是很富有那時。所以我認為，如果我們不起革命推翻這個政府，是不會有任何改變的」。 示威群眾裏有一張亞洲面孔與不同示威者交流，原來他是居於法國的香港政治哲學學者 Kenneth，自2015年就開始研究法國不同面向的抗爭，除了曾跟隨「黃背心」示威，實地作資料搜集外，亦會在不同光譜的抗爭者聚會中進行觀察。 他指法國抗爭文化向來容納不同訴求、不同聲音，但遇到有人「搶光環」時，有時出於政治現實等考量未必會選擇直接表達，「（例如）唔係話『個政黨唔代表我』就可以了結到嘅一件事，要考慮形勢等各樣嘢，未必會選擇喺公開或者媒體嘅場合咁樣出聲，然後可能喺其他嘅地方繼續做佢哋自己抗爭嘅工作，我覺得呢個位係比較 subtle（微妙）」。 另一邊廂，香港「黨媒」眼見法國示威上月底出現搶掠等情況仿似「如獲至寶」，試圖以此「唱好」香港《國安法》所帶來的「穩定」。不過 Kenneth 認為兩地示威文化不同，根本難以作類比，「其實早幾年法國都有過國安法嘅問題… 其實佢哋都有出來示威，呢啲法例哪怕係喺一個民主制度嘅社會，佢哋會擔心呢個民主制度會點樣崩塌嘅時候，其實都好多人出來示威」。 Kenneth 又提到，上街遊行甚至與警察爆發衝突，只屬於法國抗爭文化的一部分，沒有示威的日子他們亦會在書店等地方有不同的活動、聚會，一直經營著不同的抗爭群體，形容「香港抗爭文化嘅累積比法國人少」，但到2019年曾經曇花一現的同類文化實在「消失得太快」。

title: 李承鹏：习近平能不能永久连任
summary: 李承鹏（大眼哥） X @dayangelcp · Nov 5, 2026 我的油管第14期：《习近平能不能永久连任》 电影《黑社会》之龙城风云里，邓肥说：“黑社会也是有权力制约的，不能一人独大，要平衡。几十年的规矩改了，社团的叔父们一定会很不舒服。” 可中南海的叔父们，要么找马克思和毛主席报到去了，要么住进了秦城的豪华一居室，剩下的只能在特勤局监视下种种花、养养鸟、听听戏…… 如果在一家公司，他必须是董事长、总裁、CEO一肩挑；在帮派，他必须是帮主、执法长老、执棒长老一肩挑。
content: 李承鹏（大眼哥） X @dayangelcp  · Nov 5, 2026 我的油管第14期：《习近平能不能永久连任》 电影《黑社会》之龙城风云里，邓肥说：“黑社会也是有权力制约的，不能一人独大，要平衡。几十年的规矩改了，社团的叔父们一定会很不舒服。” 可中南海的叔父们，要么找马克思和毛主席报到去了，要么住进了秦城的豪华一居室，剩下的只能在特勤局监视下种种花、养养鸟、听听戏…… 如果在一家公司，他必须是董事长、总裁、CEO一肩挑；在帮派，他必须是帮主、执法长老、执棒长老一肩挑。未来权力排序不是一号人物、二号人物、三号人物……而是一号人物之下，全是打工仔。中南海权力体系不再是金字塔形状，而是倒T字形。 习近平会永久连任吗？ 党指挥枪VS枪杆子里面出政权，其实是孪生兄弟。谁当党老大，必须是枪老大，否则必然被拿下；谁是枪老大，就是党老大，你有枪别人就听话。 没有蓝玉没有年羹尧没有袁世凯，整个军队像玩乐高一样拆了拼、拼了拆。谁手里都凑不齐一支完整部队，没有中间管理层，瓜子二手车，没有中间商赚差价。 会上演《南山的部长们》吗？会有玄武门之变吗？张又侠老部下会拎着两把板斧劫法场吗？谁是“铁帽子王”？ 世界上有个独裁者困境：如果指定接班人，接班人很快成为权力副中心，独裁者权力就被稀释；如果不指定接班人，死后又要被清算。 谜一般，习主席到底有没有指定接班人——指定早了，就成了刘少奇，晚了，就成了华国锋，能力强，就是林彪，能力差，就是王洪文。毛泽东临死前一年才让华国锋当副总理兼公安部长。汉武帝临死前，才立刘弗陵为太子。康熙临终病榻前，才传位给雍正，传位诏书放在“正大光明”牌匾后面，一点都不正大光明。 《威权统治的政治学》统计：从1946到2008年，303个非正常下台的独裁者，被民众起义推翻的只有32个，10个里面不到一个。而这303个非正常下台的独裁者里，205个是被统治集团内部的人赶下台的，占三分之二以上。独裁者真正防的不是街上的民众，而是会议室里的小弟。 最刺激的是突尼斯的布尔吉巴，他独裁三十一年，精心挑选最信任的本·阿里当接班人。可一个多月后的某天夜里，本·阿里把七个医生召到内政部，让他们签字证明——老领导精神失常了。 有医生不干，本·阿里一拍桌子“老子数到三”……医生马上服软。自从得了精神病，我的精神好多了。第二天老领导被软禁在一处大宅子里，一直到死去。 未来漫长岁月，总有天意，所谓天意，就是每个人的心意。 习近平到底能不能永久连任，点击进入： 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 2h 习近平会不会永久连任？看看王莽，俩人活像孪生兄弟。年轻时都谦虚低调，恭敬节俭。俩人都心怀不忍，接济黎民百姓。俩人都具有史命感，王莽想回到“周公盛世”，习近平要“中华民族伟大复兴”。俩人都玩国进民退，百业凋敝。 王莽因为猜忌，至死没解决接班人问题。习主席已七十三岁，接班人也习惯性流产。 独裁者困境：如果指定接班人，官员们会向未来皇帝靠拢，接班人成为权力副中心，独裁者权力就被稀释；但如果不指定接班人，死后又被清算——斯大林没指定接班人，赫鲁晓夫上位后全盘否定斯大林，遗体都迁出了列宁墓。 习主席不能公开指定接班人，形成权力副中心。又必须选定可靠接班人，以免死后被翻盘。独裁者永远找不到安全交权方式。民主选举吵吵闹闹，但有基本制度保障。独裁者交班，步步惊心，杀机四伏，老命都得搭进去。 习主席当然会指定接班人，但指定早了，就成了刘少奇；晚了，成了华国锋；能力强，成了林彪；能力差，就成了王洪文。《威权统治的政治学》统计：1946到2008年303个非正常下台的独裁者，被民众起义推翻的只有32个，不到十分之一。303个非正常下台的独裁者里，205个是被统治集团内部的人赶下去的，占三分之二以上。 独裁者真正要防的，不是街上的民众，而是会议室里的小弟。 著名的例子是安哥拉独裁者多斯桑托斯，执政三十八年。2016年精心指定了接班人。没想到接班人和军队结盟。一上任就清算。逼的多斯桑托斯流亡，客死他乡。 哈萨克斯坦的纳扎尔巴耶夫，独裁三十年，2019年传位给最信任的接班人，接班人把首都改名“努尔苏丹”——纳扎尔巴耶夫的尊号。此举向老领导表忠心、向世人秀恩爱。可是秀恩爱，死得快。一年后，这名接班人就清算纳扎尔巴耶夫，还逼他公开承认自己“不过是个退休人员”。这叫杀人诛心。 摆在独裁者面前的世纪难题，你永远不知道，眼前这些忠心耿耿的接班人，李强？蔡奇？丁薛祥？哪个会突然跳出来捅你刀子。 更刺激的是突尼斯的布尔吉巴，独裁三十一年，挑选最信任的本·阿里当接班人，可一个多月后的某天夜里，本·阿里把七个医生召到内政部，让他们签字，证明老领导精神失常了。有医生不干，本.阿里一拍桌子，老子数到三…… 第二天老领导就下台了，被软禁在一处大宅子里，一直到死去。 自从得了精神病，我的精神好多了。习近平会不会永久连任？关注我的油管号： https:// youtube.com/channel/UCye2h ———————————————— wJV7IRisIcGSUpQbVw?si=UWEkRJrIAX9_mqjl 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 4h 习近平会不会永久连任，先看看他与哪位历史人物最像。他跟王莽活像孪生兄弟。  俩人年轻时都朴实谦虚。《汉书》说王莽“折节为恭俭”，能放下外戚子弟的身段，待人恭敬、节俭。王家子弟个个穿戴奢华，只有王莽穿布衣，活像穷书生。   习近平作为副国级高干子弟，十五岁到梁家河插队，住窑洞，吃粗粮，穿粗衣，身上长跳蚤，扛着锄头下地干活。跟那些北京来的知青完全不一样。   王莽乐善好施，车马皮衣都分给门客。习近平碰上个从米脂一路讨饭过来的老汉，心中不忍，把身上的钱和粮票掏光，连外套都脱下来给了老汉。   王莽替穷人办事，在长安城盖了两百所住宅，安置贫民。习近平在宁德时眼见一万三千多户船民挤在船上住，有人住在山上茅草屋。他立马在福安开现场会，让几万人搬进了新房。   为了让农民富起来，他自费学建沼气池。捅导管时，沼气喷涌而出，溅了满脸粪水。   王莽当上大司马，妻子穿着短衣布裙待客，客人还以为她是佣人。电视台来采访，彭丽媛抱着孩子，洗菜，炒菜，拖地，开饭时亲自端菜，要不是那张人人认识的脸，就是一个普通主妇。   每逢灾年，王莽只吃素，太后只得下诏，让他按时吃肉，爱惜身体。习近平冒着零下十几度严寒去看望灾区群众。晚饭只上了阜平炖菜、拍蒜茼蒿几个家常菜……   王莽上书捐钱百万、献田三十顷救济灾民，官员跟捐。疫情爆发，习近平带头捐款，全国党员官员共跟捐了116.3亿元。   俩人上位史也惊人相似。大司马王根病退前，目睹王莽种种仁义，推举他接替自己的职务。2007年曾庆红退休，深觉习近平低调憨厚，向老江推荐了习近平。王莽和习主席都以谦虚低调仁义才登得大位，都是人们发现时已无法挽回。王莽篡位后索要传国玉玺，王政君大骂王莽猪狗不如。江泽民、曾庆红后来目睹自己的人马被习一个个拿下，当年以裸退支持习上位的胡锦涛被公开架走，打碎了牙往肚里吞，权当是补钙了。   王莽为了消除贫富差距，打击土地兼并，天下田地收归国有，是为“王田”。习近平提出共同富裕，消除贫富差距，国进民退，是为“中国梦”。   王莽盐铁收归官府，滥改币制，开设官市，百姓苦不堪言。习近平肃整市场，国家队进场，百业凋敝，失业居高不下。王莽反贪，习近平反腐一直在路上。   王莽要回到周公盛世，习近平要中华民族伟大复兴。人们总说王莽是从未来穿越回汉朝的社会主义者，可谁说习总不是从两千年穿越到现在的王莽。   敬请加关注： https:// youtube.com/channel/UCye2h wJV7IRisIcGSUpQbVw?si=NIME9UtuSKr8XLgt _________________________________________ 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 5h 深改组组长，网信组组长，军改组组长，财经组长，外事组长，对台组长，足球都没放过，以前中国足球恐韩恐伊，现在连越南都踢不过。过去中国足球“问君能有几多愁，恰似一群太监上青楼”，为啥？九十分钟不射啊！现在中国足球已经“山外青山楼外楼，场上跑着十一只大马猴”——过去是能力问题，现在纯来搞笑的。   国务院沦为军机处，李克强除了泄露“中国有六亿人月收入一千元”的机密，除了临死前那句“长江黄河不会倒流”，一事无成。   到了李强连军机处都不配，就是一个秉笔太监，开会时隔着大一截，生怕惊着圣驾。国务院组织法明确写上“拥护党中央领导”，政府立法宣布效忠政党，跟朝鲜没区别了，俄罗斯表面上宪法还规定“任何意识形态不得确立为国家强制性意识形态”。   宗教局也归并进党的统战部，信神，也归党管了。现在僧人做早课，念着念着就是：观自在菩萨，行深般若波罗蜜多时，照见五蕴皆空，树立两个确立、四个意识四个自信，坚决维护习近平党中央核心，政治意识、看齐意识，道路自信、制度自信……贫僧念的不是《金刚经》《心经》，而是党章和《习近平谈治国理政》。   这世道，没有高僧，只有妖僧。   枪杆子、钱袋子、印把子、木鱼子，刀把子，笔杆子是明确写出“习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想”，人还活着把思想挂上了自己名字，老江老胡没这待遇，老邓是死后才有这待遇，跟毛泽东并肩了。   只剩一关——老人。中共有老人政治，胡耀邦、赵紫阳都是被元老们批倒的。江泽民头上有邓小平，胡锦涛头上有江泽民。到了习近平，胡锦涛裸退，老江2022年去世……我翻遍历史，少见这么好运气的上位者。 看看活着的前政治局常委：   李岚清94岁，李瑞环92岁，罗干91岁，吴官正88岁，曾庆红87岁，胡锦涛84岁，温家宝84岁……   老人手里都没兵。除了胡锦涛温家宝曾庆红王岐山，都没政治影响力，有也是负的，跳出个张高丽，人们立马联想到女子网球运动。   重要的是造反这事儿是冲动型产业，上了年纪随着睾丸酮下降就造不动了。历史上除了司马懿70岁时发动高平陵之变，李世民玄武门之变才28岁，赵匡胤陈桥兵变才33岁，朱棣起兵靖难39岁，杨坚篡北周40岁，拿破仑雾月政变才30岁。年纪大了没心思反了。当初涛哥被拖出去，手下连目送都不敢，正可谓，问君能有几多愁，恰似一群太……太阳今儿真好啊。   五中全会说：决不允许有“铁帽子王”……谁是铁帽子王，姓曾、姓温还是姓王，此言即出，必有回响。   点击进入： https:// youtu.be/t8QMw5quq8k?si =fmXg5GcCm0eylG1v ___________________________________ 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · Nov 5, 2026 造反？不是冷兵器时代了，李自成可以跟官兵刀对刀、剑对剑。现在你攒两万人上街，拿菜刀跟无人机对战？……菜刀也是上了锁的。 你以为武昌起义靠新军几个精神小伙干成的？不，湖北谘议局议长汤化龙手握一支有两千条德国毛瑟枪的民团，武器比清军还先进。起义后通电全国，力推黎元洪出任都督，革命军才没被列强当成乱匪。太平天国怎么败的，列强不支持啊。 巧了，汤化龙的弟弟汤芗铭正好是前来镇压的清军舰队一等参谋官，清军舰队总司令萨镇冰，又正好是黎元洪的老师…… 经黎元洪给老师写信，经汤芗铭运作，清军舰队炮口一转，只是对天空放了一通烟花。否则袁世凯还没来，新军就被灭了。 当时商人都很有理想，上海绅商王一亭为革命筹款几十万元，为军政府垫付四十万元公债，上海商团运了五百支快枪支援革命军光复南京。《剑桥民国史》记载，上海商团还向革命军资助了七百万两白银。 体制内，状元朗实业家张謇本是帝党，武昌起义后却第一批转向共和，主持南北议和，据说退位诏书据说就是他起草的。你能想像王沪宁老师写退位诏书吗？不可能，决对不可能。 你更想像不到，力推袁世凯复出的竟有很多清廷王公大臣，大学士那桐和徐世昌向摄政王提请起用袁世凯，庆亲王奕劻表面不吭声，背地里劝袁世凯出山。这才有了后面的事儿。 要成事儿，必须把社会各阶层各利益团体整合到一起。现在谁有能力把它们团结到一起？只有魔法才能打败魔法，只有习总才能指明方向。 独裁者规律：权力不是来自于选举而来自于分赃，所以腐败成了权力运行的原动力。可是腐败又会影响独裁者统治。所以独裁者必须反腐且只能选择性反腐，导致世风日下、经济越来越差，最后必然是全民成了代价。 官场天天反腐，经济一塌糊涂，运动此起彼伏，百姓越来越苦。 2027年国考招公务员，税务占了67.28%，每3个公务员就招俩税务。国家没钱了，之前针对富人，未来针对中产和白领，再往后针对农民和灵活就业者，人人不能幸免。肉食者有个逻辑：如果你提供不了情绪价值，就得让你提供营养价值。 当社会被逼到这个份上，就是社会各阶层各利益集团整合的最佳契机。放眼中国，谁能做到，习总，牛逼！ 点击进入： Greene) 先生就任美国在台协会 (AIT) 所长。这是格林主任第三次在台湾任职，上一次担任 AIT 副主任是在 2018 年至 2021 年期间。他最近于 2021-24 年间担任驻日本东京代表团副团长。完整传记 Judy Kuo 代理副主任 Judy Kuo 是高级外交部门的职业官员，公使衔参赞级。最近，她担任驻美国台湾协调办公室主任。
美国国务院东亚和太平洋事务局。此前，她曾担任美国驻哈萨克斯坦使团临时代办。完整传记 Matthew Cenzer 公共外交科科长 Matthew Cenzer 在接受普通话培训后于 2026 年 7 月开始担任美国在台协会公共外交科科长。在此之前，他曾担任美国驻日本名古屋领事馆首席官员。完整传记克里斯托弗·罗斯 (Christopher Rose) 领事处处长克里斯托弗·罗斯 (Christopher Rose) 于 2026 年 6 月加入美国在台协会，担任领事处处长。他最近的职务包括担任美国驻中国上海总领事馆副领事馆长和美国驻韩国首尔大使馆领事馆长。完整传记 Janée Pierre-Louis 商务科科长 Janée Pierre-Louis 是高级商务官，并担任 AIT 商务科科长。她曾担任过一系列领导职务，包括美国驻约旦安曼大使馆的高级商务官员和美国驻加拿大渥太华大使馆的副高级商务官员。完整传记 Eric Frater 经济处处长 Eric Frater 目前担任台北美国在台协会经济处处长。自 2005 年加入外交部以来，埃里克·弗雷特一直致力于推进美国的经济利益并深化与东亚盟友和伙伴的经济合作。
完整传记 迈克尔·皮纳泰罗 (Michael Pignatello) 政治处处长迈克 (Mike) 担任台北美国在台协会政治处处长。他于 2004 年加入美国国务院，曾在阿尔及尔、北京、马尼拉和台北以及纽约美国驻联合国代表团担任过各种政治、经济和领事职务。完整传记 Raymond Greene 主任 Judy Kuo 代理副主任 Matthew Cenzer 公共外交科科长 Christopher Rose 领事科科长 Janée Pi
