Department of Homeland Security Coast Guard
[Docket No. USCG-2026-1338]
Notice of proposed rulemaking.
The Coast Guard proposes to temporarily modify the operating regulation that governs the Macombs Dam Bridge across the Harlem River, mile 3.2, between the Boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City, New York. The bridge owner, New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT), submitted a request on August 31, 2026, to allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from February 1, 2027, through November 30, 2027, and facilitate rehabilitation of the bridge structure. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.
Comments and related material must be received by the Coast Guard on or before December 7, 2026.
The Coast Guard anticipates that this proposed rule will be effective from 12:01 a.m. on February 1, 2027, through 11:59 p.m. on November 30, 2027.
You may submit comments identified by docket number USCG-2026-1338 at https://www.regulations.gov.
See the “Public Participation and Request for Comments” portion of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section below for instructions on submitting comments. This notice of proposed rulemaking with its plain-language, 100-word-or-less proposed rule summary will be available in this same docket.
If you have questions on this proposed rule, call or email Donna D. Leoce, Northeast Coast Guard District, Bridge Management Specialist, telephone number (571) 613-2415, email Donna.D.Leoce@uscg.mil.
I. Table of Abbreviations
U.S.C. United States Code ( printed page 70040)
NYCDOT New York City Department of Transportation
II. Background, Purpose and Legal Basis
The Macombs Dam Bridge across the Harlem River, between the Boroughs of the Bronx and Manhattan, New York, at mile 3.2, owned and operated by NYCDOT, has a vertical clearance of 28.2 feet above mean high water when closed, unlimited when open, and a horizontal clearance of 164 feet. The proposed temporary regulation will allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from 12:01 a.m. February 1, 2027, through 11:59 p.m. November 30, 2027. The modification of the bridge schedule will allow NYCDOT to perform necessary rehabilitation to the structure of the 131-year-old bridge to ensure its safety.
Commercial vessels, including small passenger vessels and marine construction support vessels, and recreational vessels transit the Harlem River in the vicinity of the bridge. Under this proposed rule, commercial and recreational vessels that regularly use the Harlem River can still transit under the bridge in the closed position. Vessels requiring higher vertical clearance can also access the Harlem River through the waterway's confluences with the East River to the east and the Hudson River to the west. NYCDOT briefed their proposed modification of the bridge's operating schedule to the Port of New York and New Jersey Harbor Safety, Navigation, and Operations Committee. This committee, comprised of representatives of major segments of waterway users, did not object to NYCDOT's proposal.
The existing operating schedule is listed in 33 CFR 117.789(b)(1). Currently, the Macombs Dam Bridge opens on signal with at least a four-hour advance notice and does not need to open for the passage of vessel traffic from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Friday except federal holidays.
NYCDOT requests a modification of 33 CFR 117.789(b)(1) to allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from February 1, 2027, through November 30, 2027, while a work platform system is in place under the bridge deck to perform necessary structural rehabilitation. The work platform will reduce the vertical clearance of the bridge to no less than 24.5 feet above Mean High Water in the closed position. The platform will not obstruct the operation of the bridge's navigation lights.
III. Discussion of Proposed Rule
We propose to temporarily modify the drawbridge operating schedule in 33 CFR 117.789(b)(1) for the Macombs Dam Bridge, at mile 3.2. The proposed rule would allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from February 1, 2027, through November 30, 2027, while a work platform system is in place under the bridge deck to perform necessary structural rehabilitation. Commercial and recreational vessels that regularly use the Harlem River can still transit under the bridge given in the closed position. Vessels requiring higher vertical clearance can also access the Harlem River through the waterway's confluences with the East River to the east and the Hudson River to the west.
We developed this proposed rule after considering numerous statutes and Executive Orders related to rulemaking. Below we summarize our analyses based on these statutes and Executive Orders.
A. Impact on Small Entities
The Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980, 5 U.S.C. 601-612, as amended, requires Federal agencies to consider the potential impact of regulations on small entities during rulemaking. The term “small entities” comprises small businesses, not-for-profit organizations that are independently owned and operated and are not dominant in their fields, and governmental jurisdictions with populations of less than 50,000. The Coast Guard certifies under 5 U.S.C. 605(b) that this proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities for the following reasons. Commercial and recreational vessels that regularly use the Harlem River can still transit under the bridge given in the closed position. Vessels requiring higher vertical clearance can also access the Harlem River through the waterway's confluences with the East River to the east and the Hudson River to the west.
If you think that your business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction qualifies as a small entity and that this rule would have a significant economic impact on it, please submit a comment (see ADDRESSES ) explaining why you think it qualifies and how and to what degree this rule would economically affect it.
Under section 213(a) of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (Pub. L. 104-121), we want to assist small entities in understanding this proposed rule. If the proposed rule would affect your small business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction and you have questions concerning its provisions or options for compliance, please contact the person listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section. The Coast Guard will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain about this proposed rule or any policy or action of the Coast Guard.
B. Collection of Information
This proposed rule would call for no new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520.).
C. Federalism and Indian Tribal Governments
A rule has implications for federalism under Executive Order 13132 (Federalism), if it has a substantial direct effect on the States, on the relationship between the National Government and the States, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government. We have analyzed this proposed rule under that Order and have determined that it is consistent with the fundamental federalism principles and preemption requirements described in Executive Order 13132.
Also, this proposed rule does not have tribal implications under Executive Order 13175 (Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments) because it would not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes. If you believe this proposed rule has implications for federalism or Indian tribes, please contact the person listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section.
D. Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (2 U.S.C. 1531-1538) requires Federal agencies to assess the effects of their discretionary regulatory actions. In particular, the Act addresses actions that may result in the expenditure by a State, local, or tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector of $100,000,000 (adjusted for inflation) or more in any one year. Though this proposed rule will not result in such an expenditure, we do discuss the effects of this proposed rule elsewhere in this preamble.
We have analyzed this rule under Department of Homeland Security ( printed page 70041) Management Directive 023-01, Rev.1, associated implementing instructions, and Environmental Planning Policy COMDTINST 5090.1 (series), which guide the Coast Guard in complying with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) (42 U.S.C. 4321-4370f). The Coast Guard has determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment. This proposed rule promulgates the operating regulations or procedures for drawbridges. Normally such actions are categorically excluded from further review, under paragraph L49, of Appendix A, Table 1 of DHS Instruction Manual 023-01-001-01, Rev. 1.
Neither a Record of Environmental Consideration nor a Memorandum for the Record are required for this rule. We seek any comments or information that may lead to the discovery of a significant environmental impact from this proposed rule.
V. Public Participation and Request for Comments
We view public participation as essential to effective rulemaking and will consider all comments and material received during the comment period. Your comment can help shape the outcome of this rulemaking. If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for this rulemaking, indicate the specific section of this document to which each comment applies, and provide a reason for each suggestion or recommendation.
Submitting comments. We encourage you to submit comments at https://www.regulations.gov. To do so, go to https://www.regulations.gov, type USCG-2026-1338 in the search box and click “Search.” Next, look for this document in the Search Results column, and click on it. Then click on the Comment option. If your material cannot be submitted using https://www.regulations.gov, contact the person in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section of this document for alternate instructions.
Viewing material in docket. To view documents mentioned in this proposed rule as being available in the docket, find the docket as described in the previous paragraph, and then select “Supporting & Related Material” in the Document Type column. Public comments will also be placed in our online docket and can be viewed by following instructions on the https://www.regulations.gov Frequently Asked Questions web page. Also, if you go to the online docket and sign up for email alerts through the “Subscribe” option, you will be notified when comments/updates are posted, or a final rule is published.
Personal information. We accept anonymous comments. Comments we post to https://www.regulations.gov will include any personal information you have provided. For more about privacy and submissions in response to this document, see DHS's eRulemaking System of Records notice (85 FR 14226, March 11, 2020).

广告

（德国之声中文网）美国国务院周四宣布的这轮新制裁，目标涵盖了[古巴](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E6%B7%B1%E9%99%B7%E7%BB%8F%E6%B5%8E%E5%8D%B1%E6%9C%BA-%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%8F%B4%E5%8A%A9%E9%80%81%E5%A4%A7%E7%B1%B3/a-77285546)的石油和电子行业。

制裁名单中首次包括了两家[中国](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD/t-40349312)企业，美方指控它们向古巴军方提供了电子产品及其他安全设备。

中国外交部对此表示强烈反对，称这些制裁是非法的，属于典型的“长臂管辖”。

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在新闻发布会上表示：“中方坚决反对美方干涉和破坏中古合作。”

他警告称，北京将采取“一切必要措施”来维护本国企业的权益。

更多内容：[特朗普威胁要“解放或接管”古巴](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE%E5%A8%81%E8%83%81%E8%A6%81%E8%A7%A3%E6%94%BE%E6%88%96%E6%8E%A5%E7%AE%A1%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4/a-76393725)

自1月以来，华盛顿对古巴实施了破坏力极强的新制裁及石油封锁，导致古巴经济陷入瘫痪，并引发了大范围停电和生活必需品短缺。

美国总统特朗普曾暗示可能采取军事干预，以推翻古巴执政的共产党。上个月，美国国务卿还敦促古巴民众与美国情报机构开展合作。

周四被列入制裁名单的中国企业包括国有企业中国电子进出口总公司（CEIEC），以及民营企业北京华成昊普科技有限公司（Beijing H&C Technologies）。

制裁名单还涵盖了安妮·罗德里格斯·拉斯特雷斯（Any Rodriguez Lastres），她是古巴最大军方控股商业集团古巴企业管理集团（GAESA）负责人之女。

## 无电、无油也无气：古巴什么都缺

### 停电、加油站无油可加、物价飞涨，这些构成了古巴人的日常生活。在美国不断加大施压力度的同时，古巴又失去了来自委内瑞拉的油气。人们在艰难地苦熬，他们还能挺多长时间？

图像来源: Yamil Lage/AFP/Getty Images![Image 3: 古巴街头](https://static.dw.com/image/75797689_600.jpg)![Image 4: 古巴街头](https://static.dw.com/image/75797689_605.jpg)

### 严寒让危机雪上加霜

经济危机、持续不断的停电和日益减少的燃料供应正沉重打击着古巴。一场异常寒冷的寒流加剧了古巴的困境。在这个加勒比海共产主义国家，本已岌岌可危的生活状况在寒冷的天气下雪上加霜。停电、石油短缺以及来自委内瑞拉的供应中断，是古巴人民每天都要面对的难题——而且这种情况不仅仅发生在哈瓦那。

图像来源: Adalberto Roque/AFP/Getty Images![Image 5: 哈瓦那街头的妇女](https://static.dw.com/image/75807029_600.jpg)![Image 6: 哈瓦那街头的妇女](https://static.dw.com/image/75807029_605.jpg)

### 等待汽油

缺少汽油，一切都要停摆。燃料短缺导致油价飙升，古巴各地的加油站前排起了长队。停电也成了家常便饭，影响着供水、通讯和交通。人们寄希望于与美国举行谈判，但压力与日俱增。墨西哥总统辛鲍姆宣布向古巴提供新的人道主义援助。

图像来源: Ramon Espinosa/AP Photo/picture alliance![Image 7: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)![Image 8: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)

### 哈瓦那的停电日常

尽管面临政治紧张局势、国际制裁和能源短缺，许多古巴人仍在努力维持日常生活——即使是在黑暗中。

### 救急煤炭

伊格梅尔·塔马约（Igmel Tamayo）在哈瓦那郊外贩售橘子和煤炭。因为停电和天然气停止供应，当地人只好使用煤炭满足日常生活的需要。煤炭价格虽然贵，但至少还买得到。

图像来源: Norlys Perez/REUTERS![Image 11: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)![Image 12: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)

### 在家门口烤香肠

又停电了，古巴这家人只好在家门口用炭火烤香肠。

图像来源: Yamil Lage/AFP/Getty Images![Image 13: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)![Image 14: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)

### 修车修洗衣机：所有零部件都缺

汽车修理工佩德罗·罗梅罗（Pedro Romero）正在哈瓦那的路边修理汽车。修理工作困难重重：不仅汽油短缺，就连零部件也匮乏。现在即便是洗衣机坏了，居民们都要自己扛着穿过整个城市送到最近的修理店：这在危机中体现了一种可持续的理念：修理而不是购买新的。

图像来源: Norlys Perez/REUTERS![Image 15: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)![Image 16: 2019年8月30日，香港民主派社运人士黄之锋与周庭因涉嫌组织非法示威遭到逮捕后，搭乘警方押送车辆抵达香港东区裁判法院。](https://www.dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E5%8F%8D%E5%AF%B9%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A0%B4%E5%9D%8F%E5%8F%A4%E5%B7%B4%E4%B8%8E%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/a-79875276)

### 借助手机的微弱灯光

亚伊玛拉·奥法里尔（Yaimara Ofarill）在哈瓦那一家面包店上班。在店里工作时，保持良好的形象对她来说至关重要。但黎明时分化妆对她来说是个挑战。幸运的是，她的手机还能用，可以为她在镜子前提供一些光亮。情况虽然困难，但在古巴，创造力和随机应变的能力早已融入了人们的日常生活。

### 短缺是生活的常态

面包店前排起了长队。物价飞涨，物资短缺。人们只能有什么就买什么。此外，通货膨胀正在侵蚀人们的储蓄。古巴正经历着几十年来最严重的物资危机之一。

South Africa: DA Gains Black Voters, Declares Cape Town Win, but Western Cape Coalitions Loom
Coalition governments are likely in many provinces as local government election results show an increase in support for opposition parties.
DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis on Thursday at noon declared Cape Town a win for his party, and the only metro with an outright majority. Key Cape hinterland towns of Stellenbosch and Paarl (Drakenstein) remained in DA control, while in 14 other councils the DA was the leading party.
Declaring an outright victory in Cape Town with an expected 58% of the vote on Thursday, 5 November, DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis focused heavily on the party's breakthrough gains among black voters.
"One of the most exciting results for the city - over and above the overall results, we can now say without hesitation it will be the best result we have ever achieved in Cape Town's townships for the DA," said Hill-Lewis.
Boosting performance in township wards and among black South Africans more broadly has been elusive for the DA. The party long realised that without this support it would not achieve its national political ambition beyond Cape Town, the Western Cape and selected areas in KwaZulu-Natal.
The number of more than one million black voters for the DA emerged quickly as the party's federal council chairperson, Ashor Sarupen, said: "Our projections also indicate that the DA will have received more votes from black South Africans than the EFF, making us a mainstream party in every community, whether you are black, white, coloured or Indian."

content:
Tanzania Opposition Leader Lissu Cleared of Treason but Jailed for Incitement - allAfrica.com
Tanzania Opposition Leader Lissu Cleared of Treason but Jailed for Incitement
Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu.
A Tanzanian court on Friday sentenced opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in jail for inciting unrest, after earlier in the day clearing him of treason - meaning he avoided a possible death sentence. The verdict follows a disputed presidential election and a deadly crackdown on protesters, in a case that has drawn international condemnation and raised concerns about political freedom in the country.
A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's commercial capital, convicted the 58-year-old leader of the country's main opposition party, Chadema, over remarks he made calling for electoral reforms.
"We are satisfied that through his statements, the accused intended to disrupt elections and instigate violence," a judge told a courtroom packed with supporters, French news agency AFP reported.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
Lissu has been detained since April 2025. He has denied any wrongdoing, arguing that his campaign was lawful and the charges against him politically motivated.
Facing heavy security, Tanzania protesters fear repeat of election violence
His arrest came six months before the October 2025 vote, shortly after he launched a drive for changes to Tanzania's electoral system under the slogan "No Reforms, No Election".
Prosecutors argued that his statements were intended to disrupt the vote and threaten the government, amounting to treason.
Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments had been taken out of context and that he had committed no crime.
"My hope is that you will carry that heavy historical burden without bias, with courage and with the dignity carried by your judicial oaths," he told the panel in his closing arguments.
Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West
The trial drew criticism from British and European Union lawmakers, who described it as politically driven and called for Lissu's immediate release.
"The use of capital punishment against a political opponent risks turning the justice system into an instrument of political repression," they wrote in a letter to President Samia Suluhu Hassan.
Security was tightened across Dar es Salaam and around the courthouse ahead of Friday's verdict, as Lissu's supporters gathered for the hearing.
Groups were mobilising to travel to the city, police said on Wednesday, warning against "those who want to stage a coup".

Uganda: Muhoozi Announces Military Exit, Says He Will Focus On Christ
Lt Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has announced plans to retire from the military leadership position in the coming months, saying he intends to dedicate his life to Christ.
In a statement posted on his official X account, Muhoozi said he had accomplished the tasks he believed God had assigned him and was ready to hand over the office to another officer.
"My time as CDF is coming to an end. I have accomplished all the tasks my God gave me. In a few months I will handover this office to a qualified officer. I shall dedicate my life to Christ after that," he stated.
The announcement signals a possible leadership transition at the helm of the Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF), although Muhoozi did not specify a date for the handover or identify his potential successor.
Muhoozi, the son of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, has served as Uganda's military chief since March 2024, when he was appointed to replace General Wilson Mbadi.
His announcement comes amid continued public attention on his military leadership and political pronouncements, which have frequently attracted regional interest.
The UPDF has not been cited in the statement as having issued a separate announcement detailing the planned transition.

title: 5 Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP
summary: Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP - allAfrica.com Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP Ethiopia has become Africa's fifth-largest economy after revising its gros
content:
Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP - allAfrica.com
Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP
Ethiopia has become Africa's fifth-largest economy after revising its gross domestic product figures to account for sectors including digital finance, services and manufacturing. The country's economy was valued at $210.7 billion in the fiscal year ended July 2026, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa announced on November 4. The revision places Ethiopia behind South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria and Algeria, and ahead of Morocco and Kenya, based on available GDP estimates. The country previously ranked outside Africa's 5 largest economies.
The government updated the base year used to calculate GDP from 2015-16 to 2024-25, increasing the estimated size of the economy in the new base year by 59.2% to $201.4 billion from approximately $126.4 billion. In local currency, GDP for 2024-25 was revised to 24.03 trillion birr from 15.09 trillion birr. The revised figures put output at 31.86 trillion birr in 2025-26. Officials said the previous calculations no longer reflected changes in the country's economic structure, including growth in digital services, financial technology and other activities.
The revision incorporates information from an agricultural census, household surveys and data from state-owned enterprises and nonprofit institutions. Services now account for almost 36% of Ethiopia's GDP, making them the largest contributor to economic output. Agriculture represents approximately 32%, while industry accounts for 30%. The services sector includes transport, telecommunications, banking and aviation, with Ethiopian Airlines contributing to economic activity through passenger and cargo operations.
The higher GDP estimate could improve Ethiopia's reported debt indicators as the government continues restructuring its external obligations under the G20 Common Framework. A larger economy reduces debt as a percentage of GDP without changing the amount owed. Oxford Economics said the revision could improve headline debt sustainability measures, although debt repayments, foreign currency requirements and interest costs remain unchanged. The new figures could also affect calculations used by lenders, investors and international financial institutions to assess the country's finances.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
Ethiopia, Africa's second-most populous country, expects economic growth of 10.2% in the fiscal year ending July 2027. The government has introduced reforms aimed at attracting foreign investment, including opening parts of the telecommunications and banking sectors to international companies. Authorities also moved to a market-based exchange rate in 2024 under an economic reform programme supported by the International Monetary Fund. The GDP revision provides a new benchmark for measuring economic performance, government revenue and debt, although the country's ranking will depend on future growth and exchange-rate movements.
Ethiopia's rise to become Africa's fifth-largest economy shows how changes in national accounting methods can affect economic rankings without creating new output. The government's decision to update its GDP base year from 2015-16 to 2024-25 increased the estimated size of the economy by 59.2%, reflecting activities that were missing or underrepresented in earlier calculations. The revision places Ethiopia's GDP at $210.7 billion for 2025-26, ahead of Morocco and Kenya under the reported comparison. However, the increase does not mean Ethiopia produced 59.2% more goods and services overnight. Instead, the revised figures provide a different measurement of activity already taking place in the economy. The change could have implications for government finances because GDP is used to calculate debt ratios, tax revenue ratios and fiscal deficits. A larger GDP figure lowers the reported debt-to-GDP ratio even when the amount of debt remains unchanged. This may improve some indicators used by creditors and investors, but it does not reduce interest payments or foreign currency obligations. The revision could also lower measured tax revenue as a percentage of GDP, highlighting the need to expand government revenue collection. Ethiopia's economy remains dependent on agriculture and services, which together account for approximately 68% of output. Reforms involving telecommunications, banking and foreign exchange markets could create opportunities for investors as the country opens sectors that previously faced restrictions. However, Ethiopia continues to face challenges involving debt restructuring, currency availability, inflation and infrastructure investment. For investors, the next indicators will be economic growth, foreign direct investment, government revenue, export earnings and progress in debt negotiations. The revised GDP figures improve the measurement of Ethiopia's economy, but sustained growth and stronger public finances will determine whether its higher ranking translates into improved economic conditions.

Africa: All of Africa Today - November 6, 2026
Guinea-Bissau Cancels Controversial Newborn Vaccine Trial
Guinea-Bissau has cancelled a proposed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborn babies following international criticism that it was unethical and potentially exploitative. The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines. The study planned to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving the vaccine and the other half being denied the shot, despite WHO recommendations. Health experts warned that withholding the vaccine could expose babies to infection in a country where nearly one in five people has hepatitis B. The government had previously prohibited vaccine trials involving children, while police have seized a batch of vaccines from the research centre at the centre of the controversy.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
Atiku Vows to Fight Court Ruling Sidelining His 2027 Presidential Bid
Former Nigerian Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has vowed to challenge a Federal High Court ruling invalidating his nomination as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections and nullifying the party's David Mark-led leadership. Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress of using the courts to undermine his campaign, insisting that his campaign would continue despite the judgment. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council says its legal team is preparing to seek interim relief, including a stay of execution, while pursuing an appeal. The ruling followed a legal challenge by former ADC deputy chairman Nafiu Bala Gombe over the party's leadership transition.
UN Warns of Growing Drone Threats in Abyei
The United Nations has warned that drone attacks in the disputed Abyei region are adding a new dimension to security threats, following strikes that killed at least 30 people and injured about 59 in October. UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council that the attacks, the first of their kind in the area, highlight growing threats influenced by wider regional conflicts and armed groups. The warning comes amid rising tensions following deadly intercommunal clashes that killed 124 people in September. Meanwhile, the UN has raised concerns over continued drone strikes on infrastructure in Sudan, including power and water facilities, while warning that funding shortages could force the closure of a key border clinic serving about 100,000 people.
Attacks on Water Systems Triple in Conflict Zones, UNICEF Warns
Attacks on water and sanitation infrastructure in conflict zones have tripled from 2021 to 2025, putting millions of children at greater risk of disease, malnutrition and violence, according to a new UNICEF report. The report documented more than 135 attacks across 15 countries in 2025, compared with fewer than 45 incidents across eight countries in 2021. It highlights damage to water treatment plants, pipelines and other essential facilities in countries including Sudan and the Gaza Strip. UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell said that attacks on water and sanitation systems "deprive children of safe drinking water and the essential services that rely on water to function effectively". UNICEF is calling on parties to conflicts to protect water infrastructure, workers and civilians, warning that repairing damaged facilities cannot replace the protection required under international humanitarian law.
WHO Adds Two Ebola Vaccines to DR Congo Trial
The World Health Organization has announced that two additional Ebola vaccine candidates will join clinical trials in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the country battles its largest-ever outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain. The vaccines, developed by Oxford University in partnership with the Serum Institute of India and US-based Moderna, will be evaluated for the first time during an outbreak of this Ebola strain. The DR Congo has been battling a deadly outbreak of Ebola disease for nearly six months. It has become the largest in the country's history. As of 1 November, the outbreak had recorded more than 10,500 confirmed cases and 5,126 deaths. The WHO said that the new candidates could provide an important tool in controlling the outbreak, although they will require national approval before joining the ongoing trial.

Six More Bodies Found in Kenya Building Collapse
Rescue teams in Nairobi have recovered six more bodies from the rubble of a collapsed multi-storey building in the Eastleigh neighbourhood, raising the death toll from the disaster. Kamukunji MP Yusuf Hassan confirmed the latest recoveries. He expressed condolences to families still waiting for news of missing relatives. Four people were previously rescued alive. Police have maintained that multi-agency teams are supporting the operation. They urged members of the public to keep away from the affected area to allow emergency responders and specialised equipment to operate safely. The search operation remains focused on recovering those still believed to be beneath the debris.

summary: Nigeria: 'We Are Dying in Silence' - Sokoto Residents Tell Why They Trooped Out for Atiku - allAfrica.com Nigeria: 'We Are Dying in Silence' - Sokoto Residents Tell Why They Trooped Out for Atiku It was not just a campaign rally. For many r
content:
Nigeria: 'We Are Dying in Silence' - Sokoto Residents Tell Why They Trooped Out for Atiku - allAfrica.com
Nigeria: 'We Are Dying in Silence' - Sokoto Residents Tell Why They Trooped Out for Atiku
It was not just a campaign rally. For many residents who lined the road from Sultan Abubakar III International Airport to the ADC State Secretariat on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, it was a protest against hunger, insecurity and neglect.
It took the motorcade of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, about three and a half hours to cover a journey that ordinarily takes minutes, as thousands abandoned their shops, offices and farms to join the procession.
At the flag-off, Atiku restated his pledge to tackle insecurity and introduce a production-based subsidy for petroleum products refined in Nigeria to bring down the cost of living.
But on the streets, residents told LEADERSHIP in their own words on Thursday why they came out.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
Mallam Sabiu Faruk Maishanu, a resident of Sokoto metropolis, said the hardship had become unbearable.
"Atiku and the ADC are God-sent. We buy fuel for N1,800 and sometimes N2,000. It is wild; we are dying in silence. Atiku will give us back subsidy," he said.
Saidu Malunfashi, a cattle trader, said cattle rustling had destroyed his livelihood.
"Cattle rustlers, as a result of insecurity, have ended my business. This is because of the bad government of Bola Tinubu. Most people have also lost their farms. Insha Allah, he must go," he said.
Mohammed Nahuche said Governor Ahmad Aliyu had abandoned the good people of Sokoto
"Governor Aliyu of Sokoto does not deserve a second term. He has no concern for human welfare, and no projects are seen in Sokoto. He has abandoned the people of Kebbe, Rabah and Tangaza where insecurity is ravaging," he said.
A popular journalist in Sokoto, who pleaded anonymity for fear of victimisation, confided in LEADERSHIP that the ADC momentum rattled the Sokoto State Government.
"Governor Aliyu is scared of ADC. He has been asking us to help him," the journalist said.
Tajudeen Abbas, a pensioner, said he had never seen such a crowd in Sokoto.
"It took ADC three hours from the Airport to bring Atiku to the ADC State Secretariat due to the mammoth crowd. I can tell you, Atiku is taking Sokoto," Abbas said.
Atiku said Sokoto was deliberately chosen for the flag-off because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. He vowed that alleged attempts to frustrate the campaign would not stop the ADC.

The Sokoto State Government has denied any directive to frustrate the ADC. The Commissioner for Information, Sambo Danchadi, had earlier denied that hotels were asked not to accommodate ADC supporters. At the same time, the Commissioner for Lands and Housing, Nasiru Dantsoho, said the sealing of the office was over ownership issues, not politics.
The Department of State Services (DSS) has also ordered an investigation into Atiku's allegation that protesters were recruited to disrupt the rally, a claim the Service described as inconsistent with its operations.
Sokoto is a traditional APC stronghold and home to the Sultanate. The size of the crowd that welcomed Atiku and the anger expressed by ordinary residents over fuel prices, insecurity, and governance signal that 2027 in Sokoto will not be a walkover for any party.

With most of the Waterfall troop already living naturally on the mountain, fencing Simon’s Town could reduce conflict without sacrificing the baboons’ freedom.
The baboon-proof fence at Kogelfontein. Fencing Simon’s Town could keep baboons out of danger while preserving their freedom, social lives and role in the ecosystem. (Photo: Don Pinnock)
This article is an Op-Ed, short for "opposite the editorial page". Op-Eds allow authors who are not part of Daily Maverick's team of journalists to express opinions, perspectives and arguments on various issues of public interest. The views expressed are those of the author/authors and do not necessarily represent the views supported by Daily Maverick.
Justin O’Riain and Joselyn Mormile declare that there are compelling reasons to defend freedom: “Freedom enables animals to move, forage, explore, reproduce and interact with their environment in ways shaped by their evolutionary history.” I agree. The question is how we protect that freedom while addressing the dangers baboons face in residential areas.
Freedom at what cost? — a reply to Adam Cruise on Cape Peninsula baboons
Is this freedom still possible for the Waterfall and Seaforth troops? And what would secure it for them and future troops moving into the mountains behind Simon’s Town?
Let us first look at the current situation, as reported by the Cape Baboon Partnership (CBP).
The Cape Baboon Partnership report records more than half the Waterfall troop outside the urban areas for 99.7% of daylight hours. By their own measure, the majority of the troop is outside Simon’s Town for almost all of the recorded daylight hours. What are the baboons doing when they are there? Are they harassed? Are they stressed? No, they are leading normal wild baboon lives.
Here are photographs of members of the Waterfall troop on the morning of 12 October.
A male keep watch over the troop foraging in the wild (Photo: David Gaynor)Members of the Waterfall troop foraging on the mountain (Photo: David Gaynor)A relaxed Waterfall baboon (Photo: David Gaynor)
They spent the whole day on the mountain, first at Baviaanskloof and then moving up into Klawer Valley, relaxed and behaving as wild baboons. This is the part of their lives we also need to consider when weighing their welfare.
Now let’s look at how we could protect that life: humanely keeping baboons out of residential areas while retaining them as a natural troop and part of the Peninsula ecosystem. There are already successful examples on the Peninsula.
Justin O’Riain inspects the fence at Kogelfontein. (Photo: Supplied)
By the measures of success presented by the authorities, the fences at Zwaanswyk have been extremely successful at keeping baboons out of residential areas. Two different types of electric fence achieved this: the fence around Steenberg Golf Estate and the fence along Zwaanswyk Road.
So we have a troop that still spends substantial time outside the urban edge, and baboons that continue to behave naturally on the mountain. We also have a way of reducing their exposure to the residential areas where their welfare is threatened.
Fencing, promoted by Justin, Joselyn and the authorities as 100% effective in these examples, addresses the acknowledged welfare problem of baboons entering residential areas while keeping them wild and fulfilling their role in the ecosystem. To me, that offers a much more positive welfare outcome than spending the rest of their lives in a small camp, in an ever-dwindling group, as older companions die around the youngest individuals.
How, then, can the so-called sanctuary be defended as the best welfare outcome for the Waterfall and Seaforth baboons?
Surely a fence along the existing firebreak should be the outcome the authorities support. Their objections need to be considered against both the life these baboons already have, the prospect of preserving it and the prospective of impact on all future troops on the mountains above Simon’s Town.
The authorities’ objections fall into 10 areas:
Insufficient suitable natural habitat outside the fence.
Displacement into the next unfenced suburb.
Entrenched habituation and urban-ranging behaviour.
Terrain that would prevent effective exclusion.
Further delay prolonging unacceptable harm.
A fence design not demonstrated at scale.
High expenditure for an outcome expected to fail.
Continuing costs and responsibility despite private funding.
Unresolved complications on Navy land.
Environmental authorisation, consultation and opposition.
Here is why I reject those objections, and what I propose to address them.
Insufficient suitable natural habitat outside the fence
Their underlying ecological argument is that the available higher ground cannot provide a sufficiently attractive alternative to productive low-lying areas. They consider this the fundamental limitation.
Yet there is no research on the productivity of the area in question. In my experience, it contains some of the better baboon habitat on the Peninsula: wooded ravines, permanent water and Klawer Valley, an upland catchment with two dams. The Normalised Difference Vegetation Index analysis of vegetation greenness below also challenges the picture of uniformly poor habitat.
The importance the Joint Task Team places on access to habitat below 230m raises a further question about the consistency of its approach. The northern peninsula has substantially less low-lying natural land than the southern peninsula, both in area and as a proportion of the available habitat (figure below). Yet the Action Plan sets a northern population limit of 250 baboons, compared with 175 in the managed southern population, excluding the Cape Point troops.
The Joint Task Team also supports a northern fence intended to secure natural habitat for those 250 baboons. Using habitat areas shown below, this implies about 9.1 baboons per square kilometre of low-lying natural habitat in the north, compared with about 2.5 in the southern peninsula when approximately 100 Cape Point baboons are included. This illustrative comparison places nearly four times as many baboons per unit of low-lying habitat in the north.
If access to land below 230m is so critical, how does the Joint Task Team reconcile these decisions with its argument that insufficient low-lying habitat makes fencing unsuitable for the Waterfall troop? I support the northern fence, but the same ecological reasoning should be applied consistently when assessing a fence for Simon’s Town.
What evidence demonstrates that the available habitat can support the northern population, while the habitat outside the proposed Simon’s Town fence cannot support the troops concerned? This apparent inconsistency requires a clear scientific explanation, based on the food resources and accessible habitat available to each troop, before habitat suitability can reasonably be used to dismiss the fencing alternative in Simon’s Town.
The troops would move to the next unfenced suburb
From the habitat argument, they predict that even an effective, affordable fence would simply redirect Waterfall towards neighbouring settlements.
That is an assertion, but the movements I observe point in another direction. When monitors keep the whole Waterfall troop out of Simon’s Town, the baboons move southeast into the mountains, up into Klawer Valley and even over the other side towards Plateau Road, away from residential areas.
At Zwaanswyk, the troop did not spend more time in other residential areas or change its home range after the fence was installed. Nor does the Da Gama Park troop automatically move to the coast simply because low-lying land is accessible. Historically, baboons permanently occupied high ground around the dams on the main Table Mountain massif, in areas very much like Klawer Valley. The claim that these baboons must move to the next suburb needs to account for those observations.
Entrenched habituation and urban-ranging behaviour
They also argue that these particular troops have learned behaviours that are difficult or impossible to reverse, making continued pursuit of urban resources likely.
The Cape Baboon Partnership’s own data make it difficult to argue that habituation prevents Waterfall from using natural areas: for 99.7% of daylight hours, most of the troop was outside the urban edge. My experience before the first baboon monitor trials at Da Gama Park, Scarborough and Kommetjie (28 years ago) also contradicts that argument.
Baboons from those troops entered residential areas on 30 out of 31 days. Without monitors, they had spent years in these areas and showed the same levels of habituation as we see in Simon’s Town. After all, no one was making an effort to chase them out or limit access to food. Once out of town, they behaved like wild baboons: the same time budgets, the same behaviours and the same foraging.
If habituation is sufficient reason to confine or kill a troop, where does that leave Kommetjie/Slangkop, Constantia 1 and Constantia 2, mentioned in the Joint Task Team’s Action Plan as next up for removal, or the Betty’s Bay, Pringle Bay, Hermanus, Fernkloof and Vogelgat troops? The implications extend far beyond Waterfall and Seaforth.
The terrain would prevent effective exclusion
The Waterfall brief specifically identifies Admiral’s Kloof’s steep terrain, waterfall and stream as difficult to fence, and argues that monitors could not reliably control any remaining gap.
Admiral’s Kloof, called Baviaanskloof on South Africa’s official 1:50,000 map, has steep cliffs. But the proposed fence would follow the existing firebreak along the contour, which is already accessible to maintenance teams. The difficult section is about 60m across rocks and a river at the bottom. This could be dealt with by fencing across the weir.
As a manager of two game reserves who has dealt with game-proof fencing over 15,000 hectares in the Karoo Highlands, I regard this as a routine and minor challenge.
Further delay would prolong unacceptable harm
Injuries and deaths of baboons, damage to property and impacts on residents are presented as reasons to act promptly rather than wait for another intervention to be developed and tested.
I agree that delay has a welfare cost. What is disingenuous is invoking that cost now without accounting for the delays in implementing fencing over the past 20 years under the Baboon Management Team and, subsequently, the Joint Task Team. I have advocated fencing for 26 years, with their tacit agreement.
I have put forward detailed designs and costings since May 2022, shortly after the City announced its intention to withdraw monitors on 30 June 2023. That is more than four years ago. Where was the welfare concern over all that time? Why has the time needed to implement fencing become a decisive objection only now?
My particular fence design has not been demonstrated at scale
They distinguish the established exclusion-fence specification from my cheaper proposal and therefore question both its effectiveness and its quoted cost.
I have repeatedly shared the detailed design and costing, down to the last nail, with the City and the Joint Task Team since May 2022. It is not complicated and differs very little in practice from the Zwaanswyk fence.
The design consists of small-mesh game fencing on poles and droppers, 1.8 metres high and secured below ground with 12mm reinforcing bar. The physical barrier is intended to prevent passage through or underneath, forcing a baboon attempting to cross it to climb towards the 13 live wires above.
The electrical component is designed to make a baboon release its grip before it can climb over. The principle is to provide enough energy to interrupt climbing without causing injury. It is therefore not simply a question of whether a baboon is determined enough to brave the fence.
High expenditure for an outcome they expect to fail
Their financial objection is principally about value for money: substantial capital expenditure would be difficult to justify if conflict merely moved elsewhere. The Waterfall brief estimates more than R40-million.
This objection rests on the same expectation of failure discussed above. It needs to account for Waterfall’s movements when kept out of town, the experience at Zwaanswyk and the fact that Da Gama Park’s troop does not simply move to the coast.
There is also a separate question about what is being costed. I found a funder willing to cover the R6-million I had costed for the 8.3km fence along the mountainside firebreak behind Simon’s Town, removing that capital expenditure risk from the City.
Gregg Oelofse, a coastal and environmental manager with the City of Cape Town, replied that the estimated requirement was R40-million. Apart from using what I consider a highly inflated cost per kilometre, his costing included another 10km of fencing around Signal School, the South African Naval Armament Depot (Sanad) and Pine Haven, a private estate of 10 houses at the top of the Red Hill-Simon’s Town pass. This was a substantially larger project.
Full board. Life term. You can check out, but you can never leave
It did not feel like a partnership. It felt more like a shakedown of an individual donor, or a barrier set so high that spending a lot of money on a “rehabilitation centre” over the next three years would sound financially prudent.
Nevertheless, I am seeking additional donors to put R40-million towards the City’s requirements, including securing Signal School and the South African Naval Armament Depot, as well as a baboon-proof fence along Kommetjie Road between Ocean View and Capri. That would also help protect Kommetjie/Slangkop from removal and possible killing, alongside the Waterfall and Seaforth troops facing removal to the Kogelfontein camps under the Joint Task Team’s Action Plan.
My aim is to address the capital funding objection, including the additional areas the City says need protection.
Continuing costs and responsibility even with private funding
They point to retained monitors, additional protection for properties above the fence, assessment and consultation costs, and the possibility of still needing a sanctuary if the fence failed.
Conserving baboons on the Peninsula will always have costs. The purpose of the fence is to make that work more effective. My proposal would reduce access into Simon’s Town from 8.3km of open mountainside to two end sections of about 50 metres each, greatly reducing the area monitors must defend. The benefit would extend to future troops using the same landscape, for as long as the fence is maintained.
Continuing management costs must be weighed against those long-term benefits. Before rejecting fencing because captivity might eventually be necessary, the authorities must demonstrate why an attempt to preserve wild living is an unjustifiable investment. The existence of a fallback option does not establish that it should be the first choice.
Sanad and Navy properties create unresolved complications
Artillery disturbance and access to unsafe buildings are cited as difficulties in retaining Waterfall in its natural range and protecting both baboons and people.
The expanded proposal addresses access to unsafe buildings by fencing them off at Signal School and the SA Naval Armament Depot in Klawer Valley, with additional funding being sought from animal welfare organisations. Artillery disturbance is a separate issue to address with the Navy.
The proposal also includes support for upgrading the Signal School area as an important tourist site for Simon’s Town, highlighting the conservation value of naval land. These are opportunities to work with the Navy while addressing the practical problems.
A fence too far — the unintended consequences Cape Peninsula baboon management
Environmental authorisation, consultation and potential opposition
Environmental authorisation and consultation are necessary, but the time they take is an implementation issue, not evidence that fencing would fail.
Four years was ample time to make progress on these requirements. Let us not forget that the “sanctuary” also faced, and still faces, similar authorisation and consultation requirements, and arguably greater opposition. It was mooted as an option in May 2025, nearly 18 months ago.
An 18-24-month implementation period for the fence apparently “raises urgent ethical questions: Who bears responsibility for the baboon injuries and deaths, and residential property damage while we wait?” Why does the delay in establishing the so-called sanctuary not raise the same questions?
We cannot judge the welfare of the Waterfall troop only by what happens when some baboons enter town. For 99.7% of daylight hours, more than half the troop is outside the urban edge, and I have watched them feeding, socialising and living as wild baboons on the mountain.
That part of their lives has welfare value too. Removing the whole troop would take it away from all of them for the rest of their lives, confining them to a small camp where, if breeding is prevented, their social group will dwindle as older companions die. How is that the better welfare outcome if a fence can reduce the dangers of town while preserving the natural life they already have?
Why would we not choose a solution that offers greater welfare as well as conservation value, keeping baboons wild and part of a functioning ecosystem? This is bigger than Waterfall and Seaforth.
It is about the future of all baboons facing this conflict, and whether we invest in keeping them wild or keep taking their freedom away. DM

title: Taiwan says closes representative office in Papua New Guinea, blames China
zh_title: 台湾称关闭驻巴布亚新几内亚代表处，指责中国
summary: 台湾周五表示，已决定关闭驻巴布亚新几内亚代表处并撤回其工作人员，并指责中国对这个南太平洋国家的胁迫。 2021 年 10 月 6 日，台湾台北，国庆庆祝活动前，台湾国旗安装的全貌。资料照片：Walid Berrazeg/HKFP。台湾外交部表示，未来我们将向友好国家和其他有合作潜力、值得继续接触的地区配置相关资源，以进一步深化实质性合作，拓展台湾的国际空间。
content:
台湾周五表示，已决定关闭驻巴布亚新几内亚代表处并撤回其工作人员，并指责中国对这个南太平洋国家的胁迫。 2021 年 10 月 6 日，台湾台北，国庆庆祝活动前，台湾国旗安装的全貌。资料照片：Walid Berrazeg/HKFP。台湾外交部在一份声明中表示，未来我们将向友好国家和其他有合作潜力、值得继续接触的地区配置相关资源，以进一步深化实质性合作，拓展台湾的国际空间。巴布亚新几内亚7月份决定关闭台湾在首都莫尔兹比港的办事处，但台北拒绝了这一决定，引发了长达数月的争议。中国声称台湾是其领土的一部分，并反对台湾参与国际组织和与其他国家的交往，此前曾对巴布亚新几内亚的举动表示欢迎。与许多国家一样，巴布亚新几内亚与中国建立了正式外交关系，但允许台湾在莫尔兹比港设立代表处。台湾外交部周五表示，岛内民主正在“积极”关闭该办事处，撤回“所有派驻人员”，并审查和调整“双边合作关系”。
台湾表示，巴布亚新几内亚政府“最近的一系列行动”“严重破坏了双方长期合作建立的互信基础”。台湾台北，2024 年 1 月 12 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “这些行为也反映出中国持续利用政治压力和经济影响力干涉其他国家的外交决策，打压台湾的国际空间，”外交部表示。巴布亚新几内亚政府的决定再次凸显中国利用政治和经济手段干涉别国自主外交决策，破坏国际互信和公平原则。台湾此前宣布已停止从巴布亚新几内亚现货购买液化天然气，但周五该部表示也将不再与该国签署新的现货采购合同。外交部表示，台湾液化天然气采购量占巴布亚新几内亚出口量的三分之一。官方数据显示，到 2025 年，这个南太平洋国家占台湾天然气进口量的 8%，而卡塔尔（34%）、澳大利亚（33%）和美国（10%）。该部表示，台湾还将终止技术合作和援助计划，“包括医疗任务、相关奖学金和人才发展计划”。

【原文 English Original】
Taiwan said Friday it has decided to close its representative office in Papua New Guinea and withdraw its staff, blaming Chinese coercion of the South Pacific nation for the decision. General view of Taiwan flag installation ahead of National Day celebrations in Taipei, Taiwan, 06 October, 2021. File photo: Walid Berrazeg/HKFP. “In the future, we will allocate relevant resources to friendly nations and other regions with cooperative potential that warrant continued engagement, in order to further deepen substantive cooperation and expand Taiwan’s international space,” Taiwan’s foreign ministry said in a statement. The announcement comes after a months-long dispute following PNG’s decision in July to shutter Taiwan’s office in the capital Port Moresby, which Taipei rejected. China, which claims Taiwan is part of its territory and opposes the self-governed island’s participation in international organisations and exchanges with other countries, previously welcomed PNG’s move. Like many countries, PNG has formal diplomatic relations with China but had allowed Taiwan to have a representative office in the Port Moresby. Taiwan’s foreign ministry said on Friday the island democracy was “proactively” closing the office, withdrawing “all posted personnel” and reviewing and adjusting “bilateral cooperative relations”. Taiwan said “a series of recent actions” by the PNG government had “severely undermined the foundation of mutual trust built through long-term cooperation between the two sides”. Taipei, Taiwan, on January 12, 2024. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “These actions also reflect China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in the diplomatic decisions of other countries and suppress Taiwan’s international space,” the ministry said. “The Papua New Guinea government’s decision once again highlights China’s use of political and economic means to interfere with other countries’ autonomous diplomatic decision-making and to undermine international mutual trust and the principles of fairness.” Taiwan previously announced that it had stopped spot purchases of liquefied natural gas from PNG, but on Friday the ministry said it also would no longer sign new spot purchase contracts with the country. The foreign ministry said Taiwanese LNG purchases accounted for one-third of PNG’s exports. The South Pacific Nation accounted for eight percent of Taiwan’s natural gas imports in 2025, compared with Qatar (34 percent), Australia (33 percent) and the United States (10 percent), official figures show. Taiwan will also end technical cooperation and assistance programmes, “including medical missions, related scholarship and talent development programmes”, the ministry said.

title: Court rejects ex-press union head Ronson Chan’s bid to take police obstruction appeal to top court
zh_title: 法院驳回前新闻工会主席陈荣森向最高法院提起警察妨碍司法上诉的请求
summary: 香港一家法院驳回了一名前新闻工会主席对其因妨碍警察执法而被判入狱五天的定罪提出最终上诉的请求。 2023 年 9 月 6 日，香港记者协会主席陈启宗在高等法院外。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。高等法院暂委法官黄莉莉周五拒绝向香港记者协会（HKJA）前主席陈润生颁发向终审法院提出异议的证明书。陈试图推翻他在 2022 年 9 月的一次遭遇中所做出的判决，当时他
content:
香港一家法院驳回了一名前新闻工会主席对其因妨碍警察执法而被判入狱五天的定罪提出最终上诉的请求。 2023 年 9 月 6 日，香港记者协会主席陈启宗在高等法院外。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。高等法院暂委法官黄莉莉周五拒绝向香港记者协会（HKJA）前主席陈润生颁发向终审法院提出异议的证明书。陈先生于 2022 年 9 月在旺角报道业主委员会会议时拒绝向便衣警察出示身份证，因此试图推翻对他的定罪。他于 2023 年 9 月被定罪并被判处五天监禁，但在上诉期间获准保释。陈五月在上诉失败后入狱服刑——同样由黄法官主持。在寻求向最高法院上诉的证明时，陈的律师早些时候辩称，该市的《警察部队条例》是否授予警察要求身份证明的“独立权力”，是一个具有重大和普遍重要性的问题。 “没有合理的争议”，黄法官周五驳回了这一论点，并在一份中文判决书中表示，该法律“明确”授权警察拦截个人并要求提供身份证明。
法官表示，陈律师提出的论点无视明确的法律规定，实际上是试图剥夺警方索要身份证的权力。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “因此，我不认为所提出的论点是真正的法律论点。即使它是一个法律论点……我发现它没有合理的争议性，”法官写道。尽管周五作出裁决，陈仍然可以直接向终审法院上诉委员会申请上诉许可。陈先生于2021年至2024年期间担任记协主席。案发时，一名便衣警察拦住了陈先生，警察称陈先生的行为“可疑”，并要求出示他的身份证。尽管多次警告，但他拒绝这样做，随后被捕。在陈五月上诉失败并不得不服五天监禁后，记协表示“深感遗憾”，而记者无国界则表示对陈的入狱感到“愤怒”。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong court has rejected a former press union head’s bid to lodge a final appeal against his conviction for obstructing police, for which he was jailed for five days. Hong Kong Journalists Association chairperson Ronson Chan outside the High Court on Sept. 6, 2023. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Deputy High Court Judge Lily Wong on Friday refused to grant Ronson Chan, a former chair of the Hong Kong Journalists Association (HKJA), a certificate to take his challenge to the Court of Final Appeal. Chan has sought to overturn his conviction stemming from an encounter in September 2022, when he refused to show his identity card to a plainclothes police officer while reporting on a homeowners’ committee meeting in Mong Kok. He was convicted in September 2023 and sentenced to five days in jail, but was granted bail pending an appeal. Chan served the prison term after losing the appeal – also presided over by Judge Wong – in May. In seeking certification to appeal to the top court, Chan’s lawyer had earlier argued that whether the city’s Police Force Ordinance grants officers “free-standing power” to demand identity proof is a question of great and general importance. ‘Not reasonably arguable’ Judge Wong on Friday rejected the argument, saying in a Chinese-language judgment that the law was “unequivocal” in empowering police officers to stop individuals and demand proof of identity. The argument presented by Chan’s lawyer ignored clear statutory provisions and effectively sought to strip police of their power to demand an identity card, the judge said. The High Court. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I therefore do not consider the argument presented to be a genuine legal argument. Even if it were a legal argument… I find that it is not reasonably arguable,” the judge wrote. Despite Friday’s ruling, Chan can still apply directly to the Court of Final Appeal’s Appeal Committee for leave to appeal. Chan was chair of the HKJA from 2021 to 2024. At the time of the offence, Chan was stopped by a plainclothes police officer who said he was acting “suspiciously” and asked to see his identification card. He was arrested after refusing to do so despite multiple warnings. The HKJA expressed “deep regret” after Chan lost his appeal in May and had to serve his five-day prison sentence, while Reporters Without Borders said it was “outraged” by Chan’s imprisonment.

title: The ‘Invade the World, Invite the World’ Election
zh_title: “入侵世界，邀请世界”选举
summary: 政治 “入侵世界，邀请世界”的选举 如果不颠覆一个国家的政治，就无法改变一个国家的人口结构。由于选民对伊朗战争及其经济后果感到沮丧，共和党在中期选举中遭受重创，甚至包括副总统 J.D. 万斯在内的许多共和党人也承认这一点。但民主党取得如此规模的压倒性胜利是由另一个因素促成的：过去几十年来，美国的种族人口结构转型主要是由大规模移民推动的。如果只有白人投票，共和党就会有
content:
政治 “入侵世界，邀请世界”的选举 如果不颠覆一个国家的政治，就无法改变一个国家的人口结构。由于选民对伊朗战争及其经济后果感到沮丧，共和党在中期选举中遭受重创，甚至包括副总统 J.D. 万斯在内的许多共和党人也承认这一点。但民主党取得如此规模的压倒性胜利是由另一个因素促成的：过去几十年来，美国的种族人口结构转型主要是由大规模移民推动的。如果只有白人投票，共和党就会加强对参议院、众议院和州级办公室的控制。如果只有非白人投票的话，那么，连中共都会羡慕民主党的绝对统治地位。正如右翼社会评论家史蒂夫·塞勒（Steve Sailer）的名言，“入侵世界，邀请世界”，他总结了我们无能的领导层的军事和移民政策。这就是这次选举的故事。佐治亚州曾经是一个红宝石色的州，已经从 1990 年白人占绝对多数的州变成了今天白人占少数的州。因此，尽管乔治亚州白人大幅支持共和党候选人，桃州还是将乔恩·奥索夫送回参议院，并选举凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯担任州长，两人都是民主党人。德克萨斯州——传统上由共和党控制的人口最多的州——的结果更加令人震惊。但数据讲述了相同的基本情况。
德克萨斯州只有37%是白人，这也是民主党在孤星州占据主导地位的一个重要原因。倾向相当保守的德克萨斯州拉美裔不仅变蓝，而且人数众多。堪萨斯州、俄亥俄州、南卡罗来纳州，这样的例子不胜枚举，但你明白了。可以肯定的是，如果特朗普政府在过去两年里治理得更有能力——特别是如果它没有发动灾难性的伊朗战争——那么白人和非白人就不会像他们那样强烈地转向民主党，共和党也可能保住参议院。但这还不是故事的全部。美国的种族多样性为其选举奠定了背景，而这种背景对共和党人来说越来越难以驾驭。我在印刷品和网络上（以及再次在网上）指出，由于美国人口结构的变化，民主党正在走向永久多数。很少有人同意我的分析——甚至经典著作《新兴的民主多数》（2002）的作者也否认了他们书中的论点——但我毫不怀疑。如果您仍然持怀疑态度，请思考一下这两个事实：1）自赫伯特·胡佛以来，还没有共和党总统候选人赢得过任何非白人种族群体的多数选票，2）到 2045 年左右，美国将成为非白人占多数的国家。反思完了吗？这是另一个事实：两党之间白人的分歧仍然比其他种族群体更大。
由白人自由主义者和非白人组成的民主党联盟如果成立，将在美国选民变成少数派之前数年实现稳定的统治。有几个因素减缓了民主党永久多数派的出现。投票的选民比一般人口更白。红队偶尔可以赢得超过 40% 的西班牙裔美国人，这是美国最大的少数族裔群体。许多未受过大学教育的白人已经逃往共和党，部分原因是对民主党的跨性别主义等精品文化迷恋的反应。以及反多数主义机构——格里姆

【原文 English Original】
Politics The ‘Invade the World, Invite the World’ Election You can’t transform a nation’s demographics without upending its politics. The Republican Party got smacked in the midterm elections because of voter frustration over the Iran War and its economic consequences, as even many Republicans, including Vice President J.D. Vance, have acknowledged. But the scale of the Democrats’ sweeping victory was enabled by another factor: America’s racial-demographic transformation over the past several decades, driven largely by mass migration. If only whites had voted, the Republican Party would have strengthened its hold on the Senate, the House of Representatives, and state-level offices. If only nonwhites had voted, well, even the Chinese Communists would envy the Democratic Party its utter dominance. “Invade the world, invite the world,” as the right-wing social commentator Steve Sailer famously put it, summarizing our inept leadership’s military and immigration policies. That’s the story of this election. Georgia, once a ruby-red state, has gone from being supermajority white in 1990 to minority white today. So even though white Georgians favored the Republican candidates by wide margins, the Peach State sent Jon Ossoff back to the Senate and elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as governor, both Democrats. The results in Texas—the most populous state traditionally held by the GOP—were even more shocking. But the data tell the same basic story. Only 37 percent of Texans are white, which is a big reason why Democrats dominated in the Lone Star State. Texas Hispanics, who tend to be fairly conservative, not only shifted blue but turned out in large numbers. Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina, the list goes on and on, but you get the idea. To be sure, if the Trump administration had governed more competently during the past two years—and especially if it hadn’t launched the disastrous Iran War—then whites and nonwhites alike wouldn’t have swung as sharply as they did toward the Democrats, and Republicans might have held onto the Senate. But that’s not the whole story. America’s racial diversity sets the context for its elections, and that context is an increasingly difficult one for Republicans to navigate. I’ve argued in print and online (and online again) that the Democrats are heading toward a permanent majority because of America’s changing demographics. Few people agree with my analysis—and even the authors of the classic text The Emerging Democratic Majority (2002) have disavowed their book’s thesis—but I harbor little doubt. If you remain skeptical, reflect on these two facts for a while: 1) No Republican presidential candidate since Herbert Hoover has won a majority of votes from any nonwhite racial group, and 2) America will be majority nonwhite by around 2045. Done reflecting? Here’s another fact: Whites remain more divided than other racial groups between the two parties. A Democratic coalition of white liberals and nonwhites, if it holds, will achieve stable domination years before America’s electorate turns majority-minority. Several factors have slowed the emergence of a permanent Democratic majority. The voting electorate is whiter than the general population. The Red Team can occasionally win more than 40 percent of Hispanics, America’s largest minority group. Many non-college-educated whites have fled to the GOP, partly in reaction to the Democrats’ boutique cultural fixations like transgenderism. And countermajoritarian institutions—gerrymandering in the House, malapportionment in the Senate, and the electoral college—mostly benefit the Republicans. Some analysts, after Donald Trump’s dramatic victory in 2024, posited a new “multiracial coalition” that would keep the GOP in the game. It was wishful thinking. Trump made inroads with nonwhites, but he merely brought the GOP back to its George W. Bush numbers, more or less. The margin of error for Republican presidential candidates is apparently slim. In 2024, Trump mobilized blue-collar whites and did reasonably well among minorities. And yet, facing a disastrous candidate installed at the 11th hour, Trump won the popular vote by a smaller margin than Hillary Clinton in 2016. What transpired this week was a different matter altogether—an electoral backlash that some thought impossible in our age of polarization—and it will have long-lasting political consequences. The Dems will probably maintain their Senate majority over several election cycles, and if Texas just became solidly blue, Republicans won’t stand a chance at winning the White House in 2028. Of course, a permanent Democratic majority doesn’t mean an eternal one. Perhaps the Democratic Party will splinter between its moderate and progressive factions, or maybe a viable third party will emerge that, over time, replaces the GOP. On the other hand, in cities and states that long ago became majority nonwhite, the Democrats enjoy one-party rule, and governance generally suffers. A nation is its people, as right-wingers often say. And you can’t transform a nation without upending its politics. Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund
Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods
KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc.
KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.
Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.
Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:
• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School
• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School
We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.
We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.
For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.
• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities
• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses
• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers
Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.
You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.
Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.
