content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.

content:
Fundraiser by Craig De Meillon : Support Craig’s Mission to Aid Nepal Tibet Mudslide Victims
Craig’s campaign funds deployment, equipment, and communications for mudslide rescue work
Craig De Meillon is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Craig De Meillon, and I am based in Miami, Florida. I work in safety and emergency management and am a trained firefighter and EMT with professional experience responding to disasters, emergencies, and humanitarian situations.
I am raising these funds as an independent volunteer to support my deployment to the areas affected by the recent mudslides and flooding in Nepal near the China border. I am not a family member or representative of anyone affected by the disaster, nor am I collecting these funds on behalf of a government agency or other organization. I am responding independently based on my emergency-response experience and my ability to bring useful communications and search equipment into the field.
The funds raised will be used primarily to cover the direct costs of my deployment and emergency-response work. This includes my airfare and ground transportation to and within the affected region, accommodation and essential field logistics, food and other necessary expenses while deployed, and emergency-response equipment and supplies.
A significant part of the funding will also be used for search and communications capabilities. This may include purchasing or renting drones that can be used to conduct aerial searches, assess inaccessible areas, locate people who may be stranded or missing, and help response teams understand conditions on the ground. Funds will also be used for satellite communications equipment and associated Starlink service costs so that I can maintain reliable communications in areas where local telecommunications infrastructure may be damaged, unavailable, or overloaded.
Where practical, I may purchase essential supplies locally rather than transporting them from the United States. This allows funds to be used more efficiently and can also support local businesses and responders.
The primary beneficiary of this fundraiser is me, Craig De Meillon, because the funds are being raised to cover the actual expenses I incur while independently deploying and carrying out this emergency-response work. The money is not being raised for personal profit or general living expenses. It is intended to offset the costs directly associated with the mission, including travel, equipment, communications, transportation, and necessary field expenses.
Once on the ground, I will coordinate as appropriate with local emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, community leaders, and other response personnel to determine where my skills, equipment, and communications capabilities can be most useful. My role and activities may change depending on the needs identified in the affected areas and the accessibility and safety of the region.
I will keep records of mission-related expenses and provide updates throughout the deployment so donors can understand how the funds are being used and what work is being carried out on the ground.
Thank you to everyone who contributes, shares this fundraiser, or supports the response in any way. Every contribution helps make it possible for me to get the equipment, communications, and resources needed to reach affected areas and assist where I can. Flood

content:
Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.

content:
Fundraiser by Gulnisa Nazarova : Honoring My Mother Through an Uyghur Cookbook
An Uyghur cookbook project preserving recipes, stories, photos, and print costs
Gulnisa Nazarova is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Gulnisa Nazarova, and I have been an Uyghur language instructor for over 20 years. This year, as I turn 60, instead of gifts I am asking for something much closer to my heart.
My dear mother taught me how to cook. Through her hands, I learned patience, generosity, and how food carries memory. Many of the dishes she passed on come from the Uyghur tradition, a cuisine rich in history, flavor, and storytelling, yet still too little known and increasingly at risk of being forgotten.
This fundraiser supports a lifelong dream of mine: creating a cookbook dedicated to Uyghur cuisine and cultural heritage.
My connection to Uyghur culture begins with my family and upbringing. My parents and ancestors came from the Uyghur Autonomous Region, known as Eastern Turkistan to Soviet Central Asia in the mid-20th century, carrying with them their traditions, food, language, history, and stories. I grew up learning not only recipes, but also their deeper meaning — meals that bring families together, celebrations filled with memory, and dishes that carry history from one generation to the next.
Over the years, I have worked professionally to support Uyghur language and culture through teaching, writing, and sharing my knowledge with others around the world. This cookbook, however, is different. It comes directly from the heart — from meals shared with my family and from a deep desire to preserve the taste of home for future generations.
This is a personal initiative, and the funds raised will help cover:
Research and documentation of recipes and food stories
Whether you give a little or a lot, you are helping keep a culinary heritage alive.
Thank you for celebrating my 60th birthday by honoring my mother’s legacy with me.

content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

content:
Fundraiser by Nurnisa Kurban : Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

content:
Fundraiser for Silkroad Uyghur by Sarah Elder : Help our local Uyghur restaurant!
Sarah Elder is organizing this fundraiser on behalf of Silkroad Uyghur.
In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville. The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare.
Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region.
Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.'
But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia.
Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! Rehmet! (Uyghur for 'thank you')

Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。

summary: Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser. What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex
content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

Fundraiser by Kuber Poudel Chhetri : Needs for Human Right Activist
Kuber Poudel Chhetri is organizing this fundraiser.
Mr. Suk Bahadur Subba is a well known Human Rights Activist working for the politically persecuted people of the country of Bhutan. Bhutan is a country located between the boarders of India and China whose people have been persecuted for the past 25 years.
Mr. Subba is considered by the Royal Government of Bhutan to be a political dissident for fighting against the Racial Discrimination and Ethnic Cleasning of the Bhutanese People.
Mr. Subba is in desperate need of medical treatment for the transplant of both of his kidney's. We are reaching out to raise USD $ 45, 000.00 to send to India to help save the life of this man who has continually risked his own life to save the lives of hundreds of thousands of Bhutanese refugees.

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

10月，在海峡两岸颇受欢迎的台湾知名电视主持人蔡康永被媒体拍到出席竞选台北市市长的立委沉彪马的竞选活动。鉴于蔡英文在中国的受欢迎程度，他的出现很快引发了批评。现任台北市市长蒋万安邀请蔡英文参加他自己的竞选总部的落成典礼，从而化解了争议。在参加沉的竞选活动三周后，蔡英文公开表示，他从未支持台独，他的工作需要他与持有不同政治观点的人互动。第二天，他参加了蒋介石的竞选活动。
如果参加集会就等于宣布支持台湾的未来，想象一下11月28日的投票结果会如何。
执政的民进党候选人沉多年来一直在研究中国的影响力运作并促进台湾的平民准备。中国当局已以分裂国家罪名对他展开调查。国民党现任总统蒋介石在台北和上海的官员之间保持着开放的沟通渠道。北京和华盛顿可能会倾向于将沈氏的胜利解读为对独立的投票，或者将蒋介石的胜利解读为转向中国。然而，无论哪种解释都会将市政选举与台北选民未被要求投票的问题联系起来。
考虑一下沉和蒋 10 月 31 日辩论期间的一次交流。蒋要求沉解释为什么两个重建项目（一个在大同，另一个在内湖）陷入停滞。蒋将延误归因于台北松山机场附近建筑高度的限制。沉先生反驳了自己的问题：如果市政府官员知道这些限制，为什么他们不从一开始就向居民解释呢？蒋介石利用这次交流质疑他的挑战者对城市事务的指挥。反过来，沉用它来询问居民，如果他们发现障碍来得太晚而无法采取任何行动，那么专业知识对他们有什么好处。
然而，从他们激烈的交流中得到的最重要的收获不是候选人所说的话，而是他们没有说的话。中国这个两岸关系中的大象，在两个小时的辩论中一次也没有被作为关键问题提出。

In October, well-known Taiwanese television host Kevin Tsai, popular on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, was spotted by the media attending a campaign event for Puma Shen, a legislator running for mayor of Taipei. Given Tsai’s popularity in China, his appearance quickly sparked criticism. The incumbent Taipei mayor, Chiang Wan-an, helped defuse the controversy by inviting Tsai to the opening of his own campaign headquarters. Three weeks after attending Shen’s campaign event, Tsai publicly stated that he had never supported Taiwanese independence and that his work required him to interact with people holding a range of political views. The following day, he attended Chiang’s campaign event.
If attending a rally is tantamount to declaring one’s support for Taiwan’s future, imagine what will be made of the November 28 vote.
Shen, the candidate of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), has spent years studying Chinese influence operations and promoting civilian preparedness in Taiwan. Chinese authorities have opened an investigation into him on allegations of secession. Chiang, the Kuomintang (KMT) incumbent, has maintained an open channel of communication between officials in Taipei and Shanghai. Beijing and Washington may be tempted to interpret a Shen victory as a vote for independence or a Chiang victory as a turn toward China. Either interpretation, however, would link a municipal election to an issue that Taipei’s voters have not been asked to vote on.
Consider an exchange during the October 31 debate between Shen and Chiang. Chiang challenged Shen to explain why two redevelopment projects, one in Datong and the other in Neihu, had stalled. Chiang attributed the delays to restrictions on building heights near Taipei’s Songshan Airport. Shen fired back with a question of his own: If city officials knew about these restrictions, why hadn’t they explained them to residents from the outset? Chiang used the exchange to question his challenger’s command of city affairs. Shen, in turn, used it to ask what good that expertise did residents if they learned about an obstacle too late to do anything about it.
The most important takeaway from their heated exchanges, however, is not what the candidates said, but what they left unsaid. China, the elephant in the room when it comes to cross-strait relations, was not raised even once as a key issue during the two-hour debate.
That encapsulates the kind of local issues Taipei voters will actually base their decision on. Some might vote for Chiang, crediting him with moving other difficult projects forward, including one at Nanjichang Night Market. Others might favor Shen’s proposal to screen older buildings for earthquake risks and to help residents arrange repairs. Two homeowners could vote for different candidates – while holding precisely the same views about China. The election night count offers no way to tell.
Taipei’s recent electoral history illustrates the limits of interpreting local elections through the lens of national politics – and vice versa. In 2022, the city elected Chiang as mayor. Just over a year later, in the presidential election, the DPP’s Lai Ching-te carried Taipei, edging out the KMT’s Hou Yu-ih by just 641 votes. Chiang’s mayoral victory would therefore have been a poor guide to the city’s presidential preferences. There is even less reason to interpret a vote in the capital as evidence of a broader change of heart across Taiwan for or against a political party – or that party’s approach to China.
True, the result will shape national politics. Winning Taipei would give Shen a larger audience for his work on civilian defense. A second term would give Chiang greater standing within the KMT to make the case for engagement with Shanghai, and possibly Beijing. Plus, the Taipei mayorship has in the past served as a launching pad for presidential ambitions. Winning office gives a politician the chance to advance causes that may have had little to do with why voters chose him.
The election’s outcome could certainly also influence cross-strait relations. During Chiang’s tenure, the Taipei–Shanghai Twin-City Forum has kept officials from the two cities in contact. A Chiang victory would give him another term to pursue those exchanges. A Shen victory would test the conditions under which they can continue. Although Shen has criticized the forum’s value, he has said he would attend if it offered practical benefits and came without political preconditions. On October 14, Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed his offer, citing his alleged support for independence.
Suppose Shen wins, repeats his offer, and finds Shanghai unwilling to meet with him. Concluding that Taipei voters chose to sever contact would erase Beijing’s role in the decision. The reverse inference – that vote for Chiang implies approval of his engagement with Chinese officials – would be equally questionable. A Taipei resident might value Chiang’s ability to keep municipal officials talking while still opposing closer political ties. Wanting the conversation with Shanghai to continue is entirely compatible with wanting Beijing to have less say in Taiwan’s affairs.
Local governance is undoubtedly important for the stability of the Taiwan Strait. Taipei’s city government, for example, helps residents prepare for an air raid, down to practicing how to reach shelter when the sirens sound. How well the city carries out that work matters regardless of which party holds power. Still, it’s not going to be an issue that is top of mind when Taipei residents fill out their ballots.
On November 28, Taipei’s voters will choose who takes responsibility for the safety of their homes, the city’s readiness for an emergency, and its dealings with Shanghai. Beijing and Washington have good reason to pay close attention to what the next mayor does with that authority. But anyone claiming a mandate for independence or unification is looking for evidence the mayoral count cannot provide.

content:
资料照片：台湾无党籍立法委员高金素梅(左)在日本东京靖国神社前抗议，要求该神社将其祖先灵位移除。(2005年6月14日)
台湾高等检察署星期五(11月6日)起诉无党籍立法委员高金素梅和三名助理，指控高金素梅涉嫌接受中国资金约新台币1.7亿元，在台湾发展组织，违反《国家安全法》和《贪污治罪条例》。检方对高金素梅求刑14年，对疑似已偷渡出境的前办公室主任张俊杰求刑15年。高金素梅否认所有指控，并表示将在审判中提出证据，证明自己清白。
高检署星期一以被告身份传唤高金素梅，并收押两名助理，随后侦结此案。检方以《国家安全法》中“为大陆地区公务机构发展组织”罪，以及《贪污治罪条例》中“职务上行为收受贿赂”等罪嫌，起诉高金素梅等四人。
高金素梅是台湾泰雅族原住民，2001年以无党籍身份当选原住民选区立法委员至今。
高检署说，高金素梅利用立委职权，就职务上行为，尤其是反军购、两岸、外交与国防等重要议题，依中共授意指示在国会配合发声，影响议事进行，内外勾连，所犯情节极为重大，且侦查中推诿卸责，毫无悔意，建请法官从重处以有期徒刑14年。
高检署也指出，张俊杰以接受中共捐赠原乡部落建设经费为名，透过亲友账户等管道，将新台币1亿7千多万元资金汇入台湾，引进中共资源发展组织。
台湾自由时报报道，检调人员查出，高金素梅明知张俊杰长期提供巨额资金或中共直接捐赠资金为其竞选，她却涉嫌依中共官员及派遣人员授意指示，在立法院内召开反日记者会、对台湾驻日代表处质询删除预算、质询反对军购、透过程序委员会委员身份影响法案审议等，严重影响议事运作；此外，她也针对两岸、外交等议题进行抗议发声，对台湾主权完整、国家安全及社会安定造成重大危害。
台湾中央社的报道说，检调人员查出，高金素梅、其办公室前后任主任张俊杰、陈智葟及助理林怡君等4人自2005年到2016年，将其部落工作队及国会团队统合称“祖灵之邦团队”，以“一套人马，两块招牌”方式运作，由张俊杰、陈智葟同龄团队竞选、问政及联系原乡部落，林怡君则在台湾与中国大陆两边穿梭，接受中共官员指示并传达。
报道说，张俊杰今年6月即遭台北地方检察署以涉嫌诈领助理费起诉，在移到法院审理后以新台币1,000万元交保并佩戴电子手环监控行踪，但他在9月6日破坏手环逃匿，疑似已从基隆偷渡出海。
对于被高检署起诉，高金素梅当天在其脸书帐号上发表声明强调自身清白，否认起诉书中对她的所有指控。
“我没有为中共发展组织，也没有收取任何陆资，起诉书所载犯行均非事实，不能因查缉张俊杰逃亡失利，就草率起诉，转移焦点。”她说，起诉书提到她因靖国神社事件而赴日本及联合国抗议、反对军购等，都是她一贯主张，“并非中共授意，也没有任何对价，更没有一毛钱流入我的口袋。”
她也表示，将在审判中提出相关证据，捍卫自身清白，“决不妥协”。
在高金素梅被检调约谈后，北京当局指责台湾执政的民进党政府是在“操弄司法”，“罗织罪名”，破坏两岸交流合作。

陸委會主委邱垂正7日下午出席台港策進會主辦的「2026好友港節市集」開幕活動，並接受媒體聯訪。記者陳宥菘／攝影
巴布亞紐幾內亞政府要求我駐處人員限期離境並推動關閉駐處，外交部昨宣布主動關閉駐巴紐代表處，撤回所有派駐人員，並終止技術合作及援助計畫。陸委會主委邱垂正今天表示，中共無所不用其極、不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，但我們不會退縮。
邱垂正7日下午出席台港策進會主辦的「2026好友港節市集」開幕活動後接受媒體聯訪。針對我國關閉駐巴紐代表處，邱垂正表示，這就是中共再次打壓台灣外交空間的一個明證。他強調，中華民國是主權國家，與中華人民共和國互不隸屬。台灣從來不是中華人民共和國的一部分，中華人民共和國無權在國際社會代表台灣。
邱垂正強調，中共無所不用其極地不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，我們不會退縮，也不會放棄參與國際社會以及參與國際社會重要的外交活動。
邱垂正表示，政府曾經預估，中共會藉所謂國際「一中」持續地壓縮台灣的外交空間，其中一個方式就是透過支持中共的全球南方國家，要求撤除台灣的代表處、外館。但無論如何，台灣是國際間公認最善良的力量，我們願意回饋國際社會，也不會畏懼中共的無理打壓，不會因而退縮，我們會持續加強我們參與國際社會的權利。
雖然中國大陸近期與菲律賓再因南海問題起爭議，但共同打擊犯罪機制仍在運作。陸駐菲律賓使館6日發布消息指，中菲執法部門當天合作，遣返100餘名涉賭詐犯罪嫌疑人。
繼大陸神舟23號搭載首位香港女太空員升空後，神舟24號預計2026年下半年發射，大陸官方表示，此次載人飛行任務將有1名巴基斯坦太空人以載荷專家身份參加，大陸「天宮」太空站將迎來首位外籍太空員。
巴布亞紐幾內亞政府要求我駐處人員限期離境並推動關閉駐處，外交部昨宣布主動關閉駐巴紐代表處，撤回所有派駐人員，並終止技術合作及援助計畫。陸委會主委邱垂正今天表示，中共無所不用其極、不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，但我們不會退縮。
香港民主派人士黃之鋒被加判10年徒刑，陸委會主委邱垂正今天出席在台港人活動時，對黃之鋒再次表達聲援，並反問「黃之鋒何罪之有？」他強調，只要黃之鋒沒有辦法獲得無罪釋放，這永遠是香港的一大汙點。
來自中國大陸的大貓熊「平平」與「福雙」6日正式在美國亞特蘭大動物園公開亮相，大陸駐美大使謝鋒表示，這是中美落實元首會晤共識、深化人文交流的最新成果。雙方應以此為契機，拉長合作清單、縮短問題清單。
美中俄3國元首可能在深圳APEC峰會期間會晤。紐約時報分析指出，中國對雅爾達密約的負面觀感，及會談可能涉及烏克蘭戰爭、核武問題，中國國家主席習近平陷於尷尬處境。

外交部決定主動關閉駐巴布亞紐幾內亞代表處，撤回所有派駐人員。陸委會主委邱垂正今天表示，中共無所不用其極、不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，但「我們不會退縮」。
巴布亞紐幾內亞今年7月片面宣布關閉台灣駐巴紐代表處，台灣隨即以停止進口巴紐現貨天然氣因應。外交部昨天指，基於國家尊嚴、外交自主及整體國家利益，決定主動關閉駐巴布亞紐幾內亞代表處，撤回所有派駐人員，同時呼籲國際社會正視中國持續擴張政治影響力。
邱垂正今日下午出席台港策進會主辦的「2026好友港節市集」開幕活動後接受媒體聯訪。針對台灣關閉駐巴紐代表處，邱垂正表示，這就是中共再次打壓台灣外交空間的一個明證。
他表示，中華民國是主權國家，與中華人民共和國互不隸屬。台灣從來不是中華人民共和國的一部分，中華人民共和國無權在國際社會代表台灣。
邱垂正強調，中共無所不用其極地不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，「我們不會退縮」，也不會放棄參與國際社會以及參與國際社會重要的外交活動。
邱垂正表示，政府曾經預估，中共會藉所謂國際「一中」持續地壓縮台灣的外交空間，其中一個方式就是透過支持中共的全球南方國家，要求撤除台灣的代表處、外館。但無論如何，台灣是國際間公認最善良的力量，願意回饋國際社會，也不會畏懼中共的無理打壓，不會因而退縮，會持續加強台灣參與國際社會的權利。
雖然中國大陸近期與菲律賓再因南海問題起爭議，但共同打擊犯罪機制仍在運作。陸駐菲律賓使館6日發布消息指，中菲執法部門當天合作，遣返100餘名涉賭詐犯罪嫌疑人。
繼大陸神舟23號搭載首位香港女太空員升空後，神舟24號預計2026年下半年發射，大陸官方表示，此次載人飛行任務將有1名巴基斯坦太空人以載荷專家身份參加，大陸「天宮」太空站將迎來首位外籍太空員。
巴布亞紐幾內亞政府要求我駐處人員限期離境並推動關閉駐處，外交部昨宣布主動關閉駐巴紐代表處，撤回所有派駐人員，並終止技術合作及援助計畫。陸委會主委邱垂正今天表示，中共無所不用其極、不斷地阻撓跟打壓台灣的外交空間，但我們不會退縮。
香港民主派人士黃之鋒被加判10年徒刑，陸委會主委邱垂正今天出席在台港人活動時，對黃之鋒再次表達聲援，並反問「黃之鋒何罪之有？」他強調，只要黃之鋒沒有辦法獲得無罪釋放，這永遠是香港的一大汙點。
來自中國大陸的大貓熊「平平」與「福雙」6日正式在美國亞特蘭大動物園公開亮相，大陸駐美大使謝鋒表示，這是中美落實元首會晤共識、深化人文交流的最新成果。雙方應以此為契機，拉長合作清單、縮短問題清單。
美中俄3國元首可能在深圳APEC峰會期間會晤。紐約時報分析指出，中國對雅爾達密約的負面觀感，及會談可能涉及烏克蘭戰爭、核武問題，中國國家主席習近平陷於尷尬處境。

由于国际刑事法院面临美国制裁，日本计划提前向国际刑事法院缴纳会费
周五，国际刑事法院院长茜智子（中）在海牙国际刑事法院总部接受前防卫大臣中谷元（左）、前首相野田佳彦等人的鼓励。 |集集
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
政府消息人士称，鉴于美国对国际刑事法院的制裁，东京正在考虑提前向国际刑事法院缴纳 2027 年会费。
10 月，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府指定国际刑事法院实施制裁，并给予 180 天的暂停期。它已于八月宣布对国际刑事法院主席茜智子实施制裁。
如果制裁最早在明年 4 月全面实施，国际刑事法院可能会被切断以美元为基础的和解，这可能会扰乱其运营，包括员工工资支付。
日本政府官员周五表示：“如果不采取任何行动，国际刑事法院可能很快就会面临资金短缺。”
东京根据新的财政年度预算，每年四月后向国际刑事法院缴纳年度会费。
如果政府决定为 2027 年预付款，可能会将必要的资金纳入 2026 财年的第二次补充预算中。
国际刑事法院 2026 年预算总额约为 1.96 亿欧元，约合 345 亿日元。日本今年的捐款额约为46亿日元，是单个国家捐款额最多的国家。
日本国民茜已请求她的祖国尽早捐款。
日本内阁官房长官木原稔周四在新闻发布会上表示：“我们将在继续与茜总统和相关国家沟通的同时，考虑可以采取哪些金融措施。”

Japan eyes early contribution payment to ICC as court faces U.S. sanctions - The Japan Times
Japan eyes early contribution payment to ICC as court faces U.S. sanctions
International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane (center) receives words of encouragement from former Defense Minister Gen Nakatani (left), ex-Prime Minister Yoshihiko Noda and others at ICC headquarters in The Hague on Friday. | JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Tokyo is considering paying its 2027 contributions to the International Criminal Court ahead of schedule, in light of U.S. sanctions against the ICC, government sources have said.
In October, the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump designated the ICC for sanctions, giving a 180-day moratorium. It had already announced sanctions on ICC President Tomoko Akane in August.
If the sanctions are fully implemented as early as April next year, the ICC could be cut off from dollar-based settlements, potentially disrupting its operations, including staff salary payments.
“If nothing is done, the ICC could soon face a funding shortfall,” a Japanese government official said Friday.
Tokyo has paid its annual contributions to the ICC after April each year, based on its new fiscal-year budget.
If the government decides to make an advance payment for 2027, it could include the necessary funds in a second supplementary budget for fiscal 2026.
The ICC’s 2026 budget totals about €196 million, or about ¥34.5 billion. Japan contributed about ¥4.6 billion this year, the largest amount by a single country.
Akane, a Japanese national, has requested early contributions from her home country.
“We will consider what financial measures we can take while continuing to communicate with President Akane and relevant countries,” Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told a news conference Thursday.

日本挑选28个优先项目进行370万亿日元投资

消息人士周五称，政府已选择了包括半导体和人工智能在内的 28 项优先产品和技术，用于总额超过 370 万亿日元的公共和私人投资，这是其增长战略的支柱。
该名单是在当天由首相高市早苗主持的日本增长战略委员会会议上公布的。
高市在会上表示：“大规模、战略性的投资支持措施对于建立国内半导体供应链至关重要。”
这28个优先项目是从17个战略领域的62个产品和技术中选出的。预计它们将产生重大的经济溢出效应。
政府将在年底前制定实施方案，将未来五年作为密集投资期。
优先项目包括垂直和物理人工智能、数据中心、生物制药、量子计算、造船和关键矿物的精炼。

Japan picks 28 priority items for ¥370 trillion in investments - The Japan Times
Japan picks 28 priority items for ¥370 trillion in investments
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi attends a meeting of the Council for Japan's Growth Strategy at the Prime Minister's Office in Tokyo on Friday. | JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
The government has selected 28 priority products and technologies, including semiconductors and artificial intelligence, for public and private investments totaling over ¥370 trillion, which are a pillar of its growth strategy, sources said Friday.
The list was presented at the day’s meeting of the Council for Japan’s Growth Strategy, chaired by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
“Large-scale and strategic investment support measures are essential for establishing a domestic semiconductor supply chain,” Takaichi said at the meeting.
The 28 priority items were picked from 62 products and technologies in 17 strategic fields. They are expected to have significant economic spillover effects.
The government will formulate an implementation plan by the end of the year, designating the next five years as a period for intensive investments.
The priority items include vertical and physical AI, data centers, biopharmaceuticals, quantum computing, shipbuilding, and the refining of critical minerals.

WASHINGTON – A memo that circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring cited intelligence that a Chinese businessperson who had a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence.
The businessperson, Alice Huang, was recruited to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO, as part of a drive by Beijing’s top spy agency to learn more about U.S. AI chips and potentially influence the company to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China, the people said.
Jensen Huang, an influential ally of President Donald Trump’s, is a pivotal figure in the intense global competition for AI supremacy. Nvidia’s advanced chips are sought after around the world, and the company’s growth has helped drive the stock market over the past several years.

content:
特朗普和美国国会将就关税的经济成本发生冲突 - 日本时报
特朗普和美国国会将就关税的经济成本发生冲突
2025 年 4 月，唐纳德·特朗普总统在华盛顿白宫玫瑰园就关税问题发表讲话时，美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克手握一张图表。路透社
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯承诺“停止特朗普愚蠢的关税抬高美国人的物价”。即将上任的参议院财政委员会主席罗恩·怀登表示，他将重申国会对贸易政策的权威。就连德克萨斯州共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹也感叹“关税让一切都变得太贵了”。
但限制唐纳德·特朗普总统的关税权力并不容易或迅速，而且在即将上任的民主党领导的国会中，任何这样做的努力都可能会引发两党的内讧。
尽管总统在周二大选前调整了政策，但他正在酝酿一些潜在的贸易壁垒。特朗普可能会宣布一系列与工业产能过剩相关的新关税，这将影响十多个经济体的进口——甚至在民主党一月份掌权之前。

美国和伊朗在解决核问题上取得了更进一步的进展
妇女聚集在反美人士旁边周三，在美国被驱逐出伊朗 47 周年纪念日期间，一幅壁画展示了断臂的自由女神像。 |西亚通讯社/来自路透社

据一位了解谈判情况的外交官透露，美国和伊朗在结束战争的努力上正在接近取得突破，德黑兰表示愿意讨论此前未讨论过的与其核计划相关的问题。
这位因讨论敏感信息而要求匿名的外交官表示，伊朗正在研究首席调解人卡塔尔提出的与其核活动有关的提案。在此问题上的任何让步都可能导致谈判向前迈出重要一步，自六月份达成的临时和平协议破裂以来，谈判一直陷入停滞。
卡塔尔总理穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿勒萨尼周五在牛津大学接受公开采访时表示，“我们永远不会达成完美的和平协议，但你不能等待那个完美的时刻”，而牺牲达成一项好的协议。

Xi taps military ‘hatchet man’ to rebuild China’s army command
Chinese Central Military Commission Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin attends the opening session of the National People's Congress at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on March 5. | POOL / VIA AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
As Chinese leader Xi Jinping moves to rebuild a military leadership gutted by corruption purges, he’s betting that the man who oversaw the ousters can be trusted to replenish the ranks.
Zhang Shengmin, who led a sweeping corruption crackdown that sacked scores of generals in the world’s largest standing army, was promoted last week to the Communist Party’s elite Politburo. His elevation — the first made outside a congress in three decades — cemented Zhang’s authority after he this year became the only official besides Xi left on the powerful Central Military Commission.
His pick as the Politburo’s sole military member comes as Xi prepares to mark the People’s Liberation Army’s centenary in August 2027, a date by which the Chinese leader has vowed to make the armed forces more combat-ready. Ahead of that milestone and a twice-a-decade leadership reshuffle next year, Zhang is now positioned to play a central role in selecting and vetting the candidates Xi will pick from to restock the military command.

content:
香港立法会谴责外国政府对黄之锋裁决的批评 |海峡时报
香港立法会谴责外国政府批评黄之锋裁决
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
这张 2019 年照片中的香港民主活动人士黄之锋自 2020 年以来一直入狱。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 7 日，下午 01:30
更新于 2026 年 11 月 7 日 下午 03:54
香港 — — 香港立法会 (立法会) 11 月 7 日表示，谴责外国政府对根据香港国家安全法判处民主活动人士黄之锋额外 10 年监禁的批评。
立法会议员在一份声明中表示，这些批评是对香港司法制度和国家安全法的“诽谤和抹黑”，并“试图故意歪曲”黄的犯罪行为作为个人政治表达。
黄自 2020 年以来一直入狱，于 11 月 6 日根据香港国家安全法，因与外国实体勾结的罪名被判刑。
立法会发言人表示，这些批评“完全是政治操纵，旨在迷惑公众、误导香港公众和国际社会”。
立法会发言人表示，香港社会恢复稳定繁荣，各项国际商业和竞争力排名继续位居全球前列。
30 岁的黄是一群人中的一员，他们的抗议活动实际上被北京于 2020 年对这个亚洲金融中心实施的全面国家安全法宣布为非法，此前，有时还发生了暴力示威。路透社

Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong, seen here in a 2019 photo, has been behind bars since 2020.
Published Nov 07, 2026, 01:30 PM
Updated Nov 07, 2026, 03:54 PM
HONG KONG – Hong Kong’s Legislative Council (Legco) on Nov 7 said it condemns criticism by foreign governments of the sentencing of democracy activist Joshua Wong to an additional 10 years in jail under the city’s national security law.
The lawmakers said in a statement that the criticism was “defaming and smearing” Hong Kong’s judicial system and national security laws, and “attempting to deliberately distort” Wong’s criminal acts as personal political expression.
Wong, who has been behind bars since 2020, was on Nov 6 sentenced on a ​charge of collusion with foreign entities under the city’s ⁠national security law.
A Legco spokesperson said that the critics were “entirely a political manipulation aimed at confusing the public and misleading the public of Hong Kong as well as the international community”.
Hong Kong society has restored stability and prosperity, the Legco spokesperson said, adding the city has continued to rank among the top globally in various international business and competitiveness rankings.
Wong, 30, was among a group of people whose protests were effectively outlawed by a sweeping national security law Beijing imposed on the Asian financial hub in 2020, after sometimes violent demonstrations. REUTERS

summary: 台湾以中国压力为由，关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处并终止液化天然气购买海峡时报 台湾以中国压力为由，关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处并停止液化天然气购买发表于 2026 年 11 月 7 日，上午 07:24 更新于 2026 年 11 月 7 日，上午 10:26 台湾将关闭其巴布亚新几内亚代表处并停止购买液化天然气，称中国压力迫使
content:
台湾以中国压力为由，关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处并终止液化天然气购买海峡时报
台湾以中国压力为由关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处并终止液化天然气购买
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
台湾外交部表示，巴布亚新几内亚重申了之前的要求，要求员工在规定的期限内离开莫尔兹比港的办公室，并敦促关闭该办公室。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 7 日 07:24
更新于 2026 年 11 月 7 日 10:26
台湾将关闭其巴布亚新几内亚代表处并停止购买液化天然气，称中国压力迫使采取这一行动。外交部表示，巴布亚新几内亚下令员工撤离，并推动关闭。
美国表示“深感关切”，并称其为“北京对台湾及其世界各地支持者进行恐吓活动的又一个例子”。
台湾表示不会与巴布亚新几内亚签署新的现货天然气合同。它警告称，这一变化将影响巴布亚新几内亚的液化天然气出口和外汇收入。
台北 — 11 月 6 日，台湾表示，由于来自中国的压力，台湾已决定关闭在巴布亚新几内亚的代表处，并停止从巴布亚新几内亚购买液化天然气 (LNG)。
台湾外交部表示，1999 年与台湾短暂建立外交关系的巴布亚新几内亚重申了之前的要求，要求员工在规定期限内离开莫尔兹比港的办公室，并敦促关闭该办公室。
外交部在一份声明中补充说，巴布亚新几内亚的行为“反映出中国继续利用政治压力和经济影响力干涉其他国家的外交决定并打压台湾的国际空间”。
7月，巴布亚新几内亚外长表示决定关闭台湾代表处，赢得中国赞扬。
不过，该办公室在此期间仍保持开放。
美国国务院发言人表示，美国对巴布亚新几内亚单方面下令关闭该办事处的报道深感关切。
发言人补充说：“这是北京对台湾及其世界各地支持者进行恐吓活动的又一个例子。”
太平洋地区长期以来一直是中国和台湾之间的外交竞争地区，北京将台湾视为自己的领土，无权拥有国家的装饰。台湾政府拒绝接受这一立场。
巴布亚新几内亚和中国外交部均未立即回应置评请求。
台湾仅与三个太平洋岛国建立了正式外交关系：帕劳、图瓦卢和马绍尔群岛。
它还在斐济设有代表处。只有12个国家与台湾保持正式外交关系。
台湾外交部还表示，已停止通过现货市场从巴布亚新几内亚购买液化天然气，原计划2026年上半年采购约50万吨。
台湾不会与该国签署任何新的现货天然气采购合同。
台湾外交部表示，长期以来，台湾一直是巴布亚新几内亚天然气出口的重要市场，其采购量约占液化天然气出口总量的三分之一。
“因此采购政策的这一变化将对巴布亚新几内亚的天然气出口和外汇收入产生实质性影响，”它补充道。路透社

Taiwan shuts Papua New Guinea office and ends LNG buying, citing Chinese pressure
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry said Papua New Guinea had repeated previous demands that staff leave its office in Port Moresby within a set deadline and had pushed for its closure.
Published Nov 07, 2026, 07:24 AM
Updated Nov 07, 2026, 10:26 AM
Taiwan will close its Papua New Guinea representative office and stop buying LNG, saying Chinese pressure forced the move. The foreign ministry said PNG ordered staff out and pushed for closure.
The US said it was “deeply concerned” and called it “yet another example of Beijing’s intimidation campaign against Taiwan and its supporters around the world.”
Taiwan said it will not sign new spot gas contracts with PNG. It warned the change will hit PNG’s LNG exports and foreign exchange earnings.
TAIPEI – Taiwan said on Nov 6 it had decided to shut its representative office in Papua New Guinea and stop buying liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the country, blaming pressure from China.
Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry said Papua New Guinea, which briefly had diplomatic ​relations with Taiwan in 1999, had repeated previous demands that staff leave its office in Port Moresby within a set deadline and had pushed for its closure.
Papua New Guinea’s actions “reflect China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries’ diplomatic decisions and suppress Taiwan’s international space”, the Foreign Ministry added in a statement.
In July, Papua New ‌Guinea’s foreign minister said it had decided to close Taiwan’s representative office, winning praise from China.
The office had, however, remained open in the interim.
A US State Department spokesperson said the United States was deeply concerned by reports that Papua New Guinea had unilaterally ordered the office closed.
“This is yet another example of Beijing’s intimidation campaign against Taiwan and its supporters around the world,” the spokesperson added.
The Pacific has long ​been an area for diplomatic competition between China and Taiwan, which Beijing views as its ​own territory with no right to the trappings of a state. Taiwan’s government rejects that position.
Neither the Papua New Guinea nor the Chinese Foreign Ministry immediately responded to requests for comment.
Taiwan has formal diplomatic ties with only three ​Pacific Islands ⁠nations: Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands.
It also has a representative office in Fiji. Just 12 countries maintain formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry also said it had stopped buying LNG from Papua New Guinea through the spot market, which in the first half of 2026 was planned for about 500,000 tonnes.
Taiwan will not sign any new spot natural gas purchase contracts with the country, it added.
Taiwan has long been an important market for Papua New Guinea’s natural gas exports, with purchases accounting for roughly a third of total LNG exports, its Foreign Ministry said.
“So this change in procurement policy will have a substantive impact on Papua New Guinea’s natural gas exports and foreign exchange earnings,” it added. REUTERS

外交部谴责中国损害中华民国主权的言论 - 聚焦台湾
外交部谴责中方损害中华民国主权的言论
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月7日电 台湾外交部7日谴责中方发表损害中华民国主权的虚假言论，称台海两岸互不隶属的事实是无法改变的。
外交部在一份新闻稿中表示，中国国家主席习近平与加蓬总统恩圭马会谈后，中国外交部于周五发表联合声明。该声明包括中非国家重申坚持“一个中国原则”，外交部称其歪曲了联合国大会第2758号决议。
1971年通过的联合国第2758号决议没有提及台湾，只涉及中国在联合国的代表权问题。北京将该决议解释为赋予其代表台湾的权利，并声称台湾是其领土的一部分。
外交部指责中国政府多次利用双边会议向其他国家施压，要求其发表损害中华民国主权的言论。
外交部表示，中华民国是一个主权、独立的国家，从未受过中华人民共和国的统治，并补充说，只有台湾民选政府才有权在国际上，包括在联合国系统内代表其人民。
外交部还指责中国将“一个中国原则”纳入与其他国家签署的双边文件中，试图破坏国际秩序，并敦促加蓬不要落入北京的政治操纵之手。

Taipei, Nov. 7 (CNA) Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) on Saturday condemned China for making a false statement undermining the Republic of China's (ROC) sovereignty, saying that the fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait are not subordinate to each other is something that cannot be changed.
In a press release, MOFA said China's Foreign Ministry issued a joint statement on Friday following talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) and Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema. The statement included the Central African country's reaffirmation of its adherence to the "One China principle" and what MOFA described as a distortion of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758.
U.N. Resolution 2758, adopted in 1971, does not mention Taiwan and addresses only the issue of China's U.N. representation. Beijing interprets the resolution as giving it the right to represent Taiwan, which it claims as part of its territory.
MOFA accused the Chinese government of repeatedly using bilateral meetings to pressure other countries into making statements that undermine the ROC's sovereignty.
The ROC is a sovereign, independent country that has never been ruled by the People's Republic of China (PRC), the ministry said, adding that only Taiwan's democratically elected government has the right to represent its people internationally, including within the United Nations system.
MOFA also accused China of seeking to undermine the international order by inserting its "One China principle" into bilateral documents it signs with other countries, and urged Gabon not to fall for Beijing's political manipulation.

中新社台北11月7日电 台湾旅游局已将桃园国际机场为外国过境旅客提供的600新台币（18.30美元）礼券计划延长至2028年底。
政府在最近的一份声明中表示，原定于2025年11月1日至2026年10月31日运行的代金券计划已延长至2028年12月31日，或直至分配的资金用完。
该公司表示，延期的目的是鼓励过境旅客入境并在机场消费，同时使该计划与 3 号航站楼预计在 2027 年底竣工保持一致。
当局表示，该计划最初拨款新台币 2,200 万元，足以发放约 36,666 张价值新台币 600 元的代金券。截至10月31日，已发放33,525张优惠券，剩余供应预计将在11月底用完。
为确保该计划顺利进行，政府表示，计划额外印制4万张代金券，数量将根据实际发放和需求进行调整。
2025年11月1日推出“走进台湾，有礼！”持非中华民国护照经桃园国际机场转机入境台湾停留不超过24小时的旅客，可获赠新台币600元礼券。
符合条件的旅客须先在活动网站注册，抵达机场后，凭护照和联程航班登机牌到旅游局游客服务中心领取凭证。
该优惠券适用于机场内参与活动的企业，包括餐厅、免税店、纪念品商店和其他零售服务。活动网站上提供了参与企业的列表，以方便参考。
作为台湾主要的国际门户，桃园国际机场将迎来大量过境旅客，根据桃园机场公社的数据，2025 年将有 669 万人次过境旅客。

Taiwan extends airport voucher program for transit passengers to 2028
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Travelers traverse through Taoyuan International Airport to a transfer terminal in this CNA file photo for illustrative purposes
Taipei, Nov. 7 (CNA) Taiwan's Tourism Administration has extended its NT$600 (US$18.30) gift voucher program for foreign transit passengers at Taoyuan International Airport to the end of 2028.
In a recent statement, the administration said the voucher program, originally scheduled to run from Nov. 1, 2025 to Oct. 31, 2026, has been extended to Dec. 31, 2028, or until the allocated funds are exhausted.
It said the extension was intended to encourage transit passengers to enter the country and spend money at the airport, while aligning the program with the expected completion of Terminal 3 by the end of 2027.
The administration said the program was initially allocated NT$22 million, enough to issue approximately 36,666 vouchers worth NT$600 each. As of Oct. 31, 33,525 vouchers had been handed out, with the remaining supply expected to be exhausted by the end of November.
To ensure a smooth continuation of the program, the administration said it plans to print an additional 40,000 vouchers, with the amount subject to adjustment depending on actual distribution and demand.
Launched on Nov. 1, 2025, the "Enter Taiwan, Enjoy a Gift!" program offers NT$600 gift vouchers to passengers holding non-ROC passports who transit through Taoyuan International Airport and enter Taiwan for stays of up to 24 hours.
Eligible travelers must first register on the campaign website, then present their passports and boarding passes for connecting flights to collect the vouchers at the Tourism Administration's Visitor Service Centers upon arrival at the airport.
The voucher is valid at participating businesses within the airport, including restaurants, duty-free stores, souvenir shops, and other retail services. A list of participating businesses is available on the campaign website for easy reference.
As Taiwan's major international gateway, Taoyuan International Airport sees a large number of transit passengers -- 6.69 million passengers in 2025, according to the Taoyuan International Airport Corp.

大规模抛售后台湾股市市值跌至全球第七
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月7日电 据MarketCapWatch汇总的实时数据，台湾证券交易所基准指数Taiex近期遭遇大幅抛售，截至周六上午，该交易所的市值跌至全球第七位。
数据显示，台湾股市总市值为4.36万亿美元，从近期最高的第四位下滑至全球第七大市场。
美国以78.43万亿美元的市值位居全球第一，其次是中国（19.48万亿美元）、日本（7.81万亿美元）、印度（5.1万亿美元）、英国（4.7万亿美元）和加拿大（4.38万亿美元）。
据MarketCapWatch统计，全球最大的代工芯片制造商台积电(TSMC)在全球最大上市公司中排名第七，其美国存托凭证市值为1.79万亿美元。
周五，受前一天美国股市大幅下跌的影响，台交所指数暴跌 1,873.08 点，跌幅 4.51%，收于 40,000 点关口下方，报 39,701.64 点。
市场分析师表示，在民主党在美国参众两院以及在包括主要数据中心中心得克萨斯州在内的几个州的州长竞选中击败共和党候选人后，人们担心人工智能数据中心的发展可能受到限制，导致台湾和海外市场出现抛售。
据台湾证券交易所数据，本周台交所较前一周下跌 5,510.19 点，跌幅 12.19%，而当地主板总市值下跌 17.94 万亿元新台币（合 5,470 亿美元），至新台币 1,30.84 万亿元。
剔除龙头电子板块后，台指本周下跌 2,113.67 点，跌幅 7.84%。
分析师表示，在周五暴跌之前，投资者的情绪已经因担心主要云服务提供商可能无法在人工智能基础设施的大规模投资中产生足够的回报而受到打击。
本周，与人工智能发展密切相关的电子元器件行业，是内地主板上市主要行业中跌幅最大的行业，跌幅达21.60%。与此同时，生物技术行业成为避风港，跌幅最小，涨幅最大，为 1.03%，该交易所表示。
交易所表示，本周主板成交总额为新台币 4.47 万亿元，其中半导体行业成交额最高，为新台币 1.82 万亿元，其次是电子元件行业，为新台币 1.08 万亿元，计算机及周边设备行业为新台币 2,758.6 亿元。
今年以来，主板总成交额达新台币203.14万亿元，日均成交额约新台币1万亿元。
